items.title: The association between childhood exposure to inter-parental violence and depression in middle-aged and older adults: an empirical analysis from China.
items.authors: Li D, Li W, Zhang W, Zhang T, Liu Z, Su M, Guo X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The association between exposure to inter-parental violence (IPV) and depression remains to be further explored. This study aimed to explore the association between childhood exposure to IPV and depression in middle-aged and older adults, and to explore the mediating roles between the two.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using data from the 2011, 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), and the 2014 Life History Survey Questionnaire. Generalized estimating equation was used to investigate the relationship between childhood exposure to IPV and depression in middle-aged and older adults, the bootstrap method was used to analyse the mediating roles between the two, and multi-group analysis was used to examine the gender differences in their relationship.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 9,909 sample were included in the study. This study found 18.6% of the sample exposure to IPV in childhood. IPV was positively associated with depression (β = 0.804,95%CI: 0.592,1.015), father-to-mother violence was positively associated with depression (β = 0.777,95%CI: 0.564,0.991), mother-to-father violence was positively associated with depression (β = 0.796,95%CI: 0.434,1.157), and father-and-mother violence was positively associated with depression (β = 0.731,95%CI: 0.351,1.112). IPV and depression may operate partly through smoking and drinking. The association between IPV and depression (P = 0.017), and between father-to-mother violence and depression (P = 0.023), were both weaker among males than among females.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Childhood exposure to IPV was positively associated with depression in middle-aged and older adults. The association between IPV and depression may operate partly through smoking and drinking. The associations between IPV and depression, and between father-to-mother violence and depression, were stronger among female respondents. There is a need to pay attention to depression among those who exposure to IPV in childhood.

items.title: Various ambient air pollutants, residential greenness, and risk of substance use disorders: a population-based cohort study.
items.authors: Liu H, Cheng B, Wei W, Qin L, Zhang F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Air pollution is a recognized contributor to the global burden of disease, but its association with incident substance use disorders (SUD) remains poorly characterized. Whether residential greenness modifies this association is also unclear. We addressed both questions in a large prospective cohort.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analyzed 247,138 UK Biobank participants without SUD at baseline. Five ambient air pollutants (PM_2.5, PM_2.5-10, PM_10, NO_2, NO_X) and three measures of 300-m residential greenness (green space, domestic garden, natural environment) were modelled using Land Use Regression and the 2005-2007 Land Cover Map. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Effect modification by greenness was tested using cross-product terms and likelihood-ratio tests. Sensitivity analyses restricted to long-term residents, used alternative outcome definitions (F10-F19 and F11-F19), and recomputed greenness at a 1000-m buffer.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Over a median follow-up of 10.9 years, 4,982 participants developed SUD. All five air pollutants were positively associated with incident SUD in fully adjusted models. PM_2.5 showed the strongest effect (HR = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.081-1.142), followed by PM_10 (HR = 1.070, 95% CI: 1.054-1.086). Green space (HR = 0.997, 95% CI: 0.996-0.998) and natural environment (HR = 0.997, 95% CI: 0.995-0.998) were inversely associated. Domestic garden attenuated the pollutant associations in the high-exposure subgroup, with cross-product terms of 0.979 (95% CI: 0.963-0.996) for PM_2.5 and 0.987 (95% CI: 0.980-0.995) for PM_10. The positive air-pollution associations were strongest among males, participants aged ≥ 65 years, and individuals with a history of smoking.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Long-term exposure to ambient air pollutants was associated with a higher risk of incident SUD, and residential greenness showed protective associations. These patterns were most pronounced in older males and in individuals with a smoking history. The findings support integrating greenness exposure into environmental frameworks for SUD prevention.

items.title: Alcohol use disorder, heavy drinking, and binge drinking among adolescents and young adults that are "Not in Employment, Education or Training": a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Eyraud C, Collin C, Dumas A, Alberti C, Martin P, Le Roux E.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In 2022, 12.7% of individuals aged 15-to-29 years old in OECD countries were Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEET). Two existing systematic reviews have studied alcohol use in relation to NEET status, with one showing that young people with NEET status (YP-NEET) are at a higher risk of alcohol consumption. However, they did not explore how findings varied based on different NEET subgroups nor the diverse patterns of problematic drinking (e.g. alcohol use disorder (AUD), heavy drinking, binge drinking). Both are essential for understanding consumption behaviours and informing future prevention strategies. This study aimed to analyse problematic drinking among YP-NEET, considering their diverse drinking patterns and group heterogeneity compared to their peers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines. The included articles were observational studies examining the associations between different NEET profiles and problematic drinking patterns (i.e. AUD, heavy drinking, and binge drinking) compared to their peers (i.e. students or employed youth).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Twenty-three studies were analysed, including a total of 518,533 individuals. The prevalence of each consumption pattern was higher for YP-NEET compared to their peers of the same age. NEET status was significantly associated with AUD (cOR = 1.35, 95%CI = 1.16-1.56) but neither with heavy drinking (cOR = 1.28, 95%CI = 0.74-2.22) nor binge drinking (cOR = 1.19, 95%CI = 0.97-1.48). The most represented NEET profile and the one with the highest level of AUD was the group of unemployed youth.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This study highlighted an increased risk of AUD among YP-NEET and high prevalence rates of heavy and binge drinking. However, a critical methodological concern is that standard AUD diagnostic criteria may lack construct validity for YP-NEET, as they include items related to occupational and social dysfunction altered by the NEET status itself. Addressing these measurement challenges, while considering consumption patterns and the diversity of NEET profiles, is crucial for developing effective, adapted, and evidence-based alcohol prevention intervention.

items.title: Association of antenatal perceived stress and depressive symptoms with birth weight and gestational age: a prospective cohort study within the Action Against Stunting Hub, India.
items.authors: Thomas J, Fernandez Rao S, Dasi T, Gunturu M, Chilumula M, Augustine LF, Mahajan H, Davies-Kershaw H, Heffernan C, Rudhra A, Banjara SK, Challa S, Kulkarni B, Pullakhandam R, Palika R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Evidence on the association of pregnancy specific perceived stress and depressive symptoms with adverse birth outcomes, including preterm birth (PTB) and low birth weight (LBW), remains limited and inconsistent in India.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of elevated perceived stress and elevated depressive symptoms during the third trimester of pregnancy and examine their associations with birth weight, gestational age, low birth weight (LBW), and preterm birth (PTB) in an Indian cohort.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A prospective cohort study was conducted within the Action Against Stunting Hub mother child cohort in Hyderabad, India between June 2021 and December 2022. Of the 717 pregnant women enrolled in their third trimester, 616 with available psychosocial data were included in the analysis. Perceived stress, depressive symptom scores and social support were assessed using Perceived Stress Scale 10(PSS-10), Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Multidimensional Scale for Perceived Social Support (MSPSS) respectively. Gestational age was determined using a hierarchical approach and birth weight was measured within 12 h of delivery. Associations between maternal perceived stress and depressive symptoms scores with birth outcomes were examined using descriptive statistics and multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses ( p < 0.05).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of elevated perceived stress and elevated depressive symptoms among pregnant women during the third trimester was 17.4 and 21.4%, respectively. After adjusting for covariates, each one-point increase in maternal perceived stress score (β = -5.84 g (95%CI -11.49, -0.19, p = 0.04)) and depressive symptom scores (β = -7.45g (95%CI -13.72, -1.17, p = 0.02)) was significantly associated with lower birth weight, but not with gestational age. However, no association between maternal perceived stress and depressive symptom scores was observed with either LBW and PTB using multivariable logistic regression.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Third trimester maternal perceived stress and depressive symptom scores were associated with modest reductions in birth weight but not with gestational age, LBW, or PTB. Although the observed effect on birth weight was small, these findings highlight the importance of recognizing and addressing maternal psychological well being during antenatal care.

items.title: Psychological symptom burden in older dermatology outpatients: clinical, social, and medication-related associations.
items.authors: Cansel N, Gençoğlu Ş.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common in older adults with dermatological conditions, but their multidimensional correlates remain unclear. This study aimed to determine the frequency of clinically significant anxiety and depressive symptoms and examine associated social, psychiatric, medication-related, and dermatological factors.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This prospective cross-sectional study included 300 patients aged ≥ 65 years consecutively recruited from the Dermatology Outpatient Clinic of Malatya Turgut Özal University Faculty of Medicine between January and March 2026. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Turkish Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). HADS-A > 10 and HADS-D > 7 defined clinically significant anxiety and depressive symptoms, respectively. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations after adjustment for prespecified measured covariates, with polypharmacy evaluated separately in sensitivity analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Clinically significant anxiety and depressive symptoms were identified in 36.7% and 43.3% of participants, respectively. After adjustment for the measured covariates included in the models, clinically significant anxiety symptoms were associated with psychiatric history (OR = 2.08, p = 0.013), total medication count (OR = 1.25 per medication, p < 0.001), and visible skin involvement (OR = 1.76, p = 0.031). Clinically significant depressive symptoms were associated with living alone (OR = 2.32, p = 0.003), psychiatric history (OR = 2.89, p < 0.001), and total medication count (OR = 1.25 per medication, p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Clinically significant anxiety and depressive symptoms were frequent among older dermatology outpatients and were associated with psychiatric history, medication burden, and living arrangement. Visible skin involvement was associated with anxiety symptoms in the primary model, although this association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant in the additional sensitivity analysis. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations rather than causal effects.

items.title: Trends and seasonal patterns in suicide and traffic accident mortality among youth in Hungary, 2000-2024: a nationwide population-based study.
items.authors: Urfi ZG, Nyári TA, Lantos T.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: External causes of death represent the leading causes of mortality among adolescents and young adults. This study aimed to investigate long-term, seasonal patterns, and regional disparities in mortality from external causes among individuals aged 15-24 years in Hungary between 2000 and 2024, including comparisons between the pre-pandemic (2000-2019) and pandemic (2020-2024) periods.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Nationwide data on monthly and annual mortality from external causes (ICD-10: V01-Y89) were obtained from the Dissemination Database of the Hungarian Central Statistical Office for 2000-2024. Analyses focused on the two leading causes of external mortality in this age group: suicide and self-harm (X60-X84, Y87.0) and traffic accidents (V01-V99). Mortality rates were calculated using corresponding population data stratified by sex, age group, and region. Annual and seasonal trends were analysed using negative binomial regression models with population offsets. Results are presented as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Between 2000 and 2024, 7,209 deaths from external causes were recorded among individuals aged 15-24 years (79% males). Significant declining trends were observed in overall external-cause mortality (IRR = 0.97; 95% CI: 0.96-0.97; p < 0.001), suicide (IRR = 0.98; 95% CI: 0.97-0.98; p < 0.001), and traffic accident mortality (IRR = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.94-0.95; p < 0.001). items.title: The association between adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and lifestyle factors: findings from the UK Biobank.
items.authors: Kozin Porat M, Aronis A, Weinstein G.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder, with diagnosis persisting in adulthood in up to 55% of cases. The association of ADHD with health-related behaviors in middle-aged and older adults remains relatively underexplored. We examined the relationship between ADHD in later adulthood and nutritional and lifestyle factors.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included UK Biobank participants aged 40 years and older. Individuals reporting ADHD diagnosis were compared to age- and sex-matched individuals with a ratio of 1:10. Multivariate linear, logistic and multinominal regression models were used to assess the relationship of ADHD diagnosis with lifestyle factors, adjusting for sex, age, education, BMI, sleeplessness, alcohol intake, smoking and physical activity. Interaction with age and sex were additionally tested.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The sample included 133 individuals with ADHD diagnosis and 1330 in the comparison group (mean age 56.0 ± 7.9 years, 42.8% men). After adjusting for potential confounders, ADHD was significantly associated with higher likelihood of being a former or current smoker (OR [95% CI], 2.2 [1.4, 3.3]; p < .001; 2.2 [1.2, 4]; p = .02 respectively), increased alcohol intake (OR [95% CI] 1.8 [1.1, 3]; p=.01), and higher energy intake (β [SE], 0.7 [0.4]; p < .001). The association between ADHD and smoking was stronger among men compared to women (p-for interaction=0.006). No significant associations were found between ADHD diagnosis and adherence to the Mediterranean diet or physical activity.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Our findings, which demonstrate associations between adult ADHD diagnosis and health-related behaviors, underscore the need for tailored health promotion strategies to mitigate long-term health risks in this population.

items.title: The impact of cognitive behavioral therapy and third-wave therapies on the quality of life of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Wang Z, Tan Y, Wang Y, Li W, Yuan Y, Li P.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and third-wave therapies on the quality of life of patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library databases, up until June 20, 2026, to identify randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that used quality of life as an outcome measure. Quality assessment was performed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias Assessment Tool. Meta-analysis was conducted using Stata 18.0 software, and subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses and tests for publication bias were performed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 13 randomised controlled trials (N = 1,324) were included. The meta-analysis revealed that CBT and third-wave therapies improve quality of life in patients with OCD (SMD = 0.18, 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.29, P = 0.004), with no overall heterogeneity (I² = 0.0%). The results of sensitivity analyses were stable, and the risk of publication bias was low. Subgroup analyses indicated that CBT and third-wave therapies were effective in improving quality of life in non-European countries, early studies (≤ 2020), short-term interventions (≤ 12 weeks), adult populations, standard CBT, third-wave therapies, active control groups, and subjective experience/satisfaction scales; however, statistical significance was not achieved in some subgroups. Since the differences between subgroups aren't significant, the subgroup analysis is just exploratory, so the results should be interpreted with caution.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: CBT and third-wave therapies can improve the quality of life of patients with OCD to a certain extent, but the overall effect is modest. Future research should be larger in scale, multi-center, and prospective. It's also necessary to further clarify the mechanisms behind different intervention modules, optimize intervention plans, and improve long-term follow-up, so that we can provide stronger evidence to support clinical practice.

items.title: Exposure to workplace and domestic violence as differential risk factors for stress and depression.
items.authors: Lanchimba C, Courtois R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Exposure to interpersonal violence is a well-established determinant of poor mental health. However, violence often occurs across multiple life domains rather than in isolation, and its psychological consequences may differ depending on the context and outcome considered. This study adopts a multicontextual clinical perspective to examine the associations between exposure to workplace violence, intimate partner violence, and domestic violence, and two related but distinct mental health outcomes: perceived stress and depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were obtained from a cross-sectional survey of Ecuadorian adults (N = 686). Perceived stress was analyzed using generalized linear models with a Gamma distribution to account for skewness, while depressive symptoms were examined using robust regression models to address non-normality and the presence of extreme values. Multivariate models included sociodemographic controls and interaction terms to assess gender differences and the co-occurrence of violence across contexts.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Exposure to workplace violence was significantly associated with higher levels of perceived stress and depressive symptoms, with a stronger association observed for depression. Domestic violence emerged as the most robust predictor of depressive symptoms and was also significantly related to perceived stress. In contrast, intimate partner violence was not significantly associated with either outcome in multivariate analyses. Importantly, the co-occurrence of domestic and workplace violence was associated with markedly higher levels of depressive symptoms, exceeding the effects of each form of violence considered separately, consistent with a vulnerability accumulation model. Women reported higher overall levels of stress and depressive symptoms, although gender interactions varied across violence contexts.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings underscore the importance of conceptualizing interpersonal violence as a multicontextual phenomenon and of distinguishing between stress and depression when assessing violence-related psychological distress. Cumulative exposure to violence across private and occupational settings appears to be a critical marker of heightened vulnerability to depressive symptomatology, with important implications for clinical assessment, prevention strategies, and public health interventions.

items.title: Chemsex as a challenge for emergency medical teams: a narrative review.
items.authors: Czapla M, Griesmann K, Juárez-Vela R, Martinez-Sabater A, Lee CS, Karniej P, Pietrzykowski Ł, Mickiewicz A, Kędzierski K, Wojciechowski J, Raczyński A, Smereka J.

sections.text: Chemsex, defined as the intentional use of psychoactive substances before or during sexual activity, has emerged as an important public health concern and an increasingly relevant challenge for emergency medical services (EMS). Although most frequently described among men who have sex with men, sexualized substance use is increasingly reported among heterosexual men and women, indicating a broader at-risk population. Commonly used substances include methamphetamine, mephedrone, gamma-hydroxybutyrate/gamma-butyrolactone (GHB/GBL), alkyl nitrites, and other psychoactive agents, frequently used in combination during prolonged sexual sessions. Such practices are associated with a wide spectrum of acute complications, including agitation, psychosis, hyperthermia, cardiovascular instability, respiratory depression, altered consciousness, and mixed toxidromic presentations. This narrative review examines current evidence regarding chemsex-associated emergencies from a prehospital and emergency medicine perspective. Particular attention is given to syndromic clinical presentations, including hyperstimulatory syndromes, behavioral disturbances, acute GHB/GBL toxicity, and polysubstance-related emergencies. Operational challenges relevant to EMS teams, including scene safety, communication barriers, stigma, occupational risks associated with slamsex, and management of agitated patients, are also discussed. Chemsex-related emergencies share many clinical features with other substance-related emergencies. However, recognition of the sexualized substance use context may provide additional information relevant to prehospital assessment, including intentional drug combinations, repeated dosing, potential drug interactions, communication barriers, and occupational safety considerations. A syndromic approach focused on recognition of dominant clinical patterns rather than identification of individual substances may therefore provide the most practical framework for prehospital assessment and management. Although chemsex-associated emergencies are documented, evidence regarding their frequency and trends remains limited, particularly in prehospital settings. Further research is needed to support the development of evidence-based prehospital protocols, educational initiatives, and integrated care pathways.

items.title: Symptom network structure of anxiety, depression, and stress among Chinese adolescents: a large-scale cross-sectional study in Fujian Province.
items.authors: Rao W, Lin Z, Jiang H, Wu Y, Jiang J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety, depression, and stress are highly prevalent mental health problems among adolescents. This study aims to employ network analysis methods to investigate the relationships of anxiety, depression, and stress symptoms among middle and high school students in Fujian, China.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 57,739 students were included in this study. The Depression Anxiety Stress Scales for Youth (DASS-Y) were used among adolescents. Symptom networks were estimated using regularized Gaussian graphical models with EBICglasso. The stability and precision of the network were assessed by the bootstrap method. Network comparison were performed to exam potential differences by gender, educational stage, and hobby status.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: "I hated myself" (Depression5) emerged as the highest mean score symptom. "I felt like I was about to panic" (Anxiety5) and "I found it difficult to relax" (Stress5) were bridge symptoms, showing strong cross-domain connectivity. "I was stressing about lots of things" (Stress3) not only displayed the high centrality in the context of intensity, but also was a bridge symptom. Bootstrap analyses indicated the acceptable precision of edge-weight estimates with and good stability of both strength and bridge strength estimates. Comparison of the networks between adolescents with and without hobby revealed the significant differences in network global strength (absolute difference = 0.38, p  = 0.048).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Anxiety, depression, and stress symptoms are highly interactive with each other in adolescents. The central and bridge symptoms identified in the network, together with the observed subgroup patterns, provide descriptive evidence and may contribute to future longitudinal and intervention studies.

items.title: Establishing cut-off values on COPSOQ scales using depressive symptoms as criterion: a longitudinal study with a random sample of employees in Germany.
items.authors: Schäfers R, Conway PM, Burr H, Rose U.
items.journal: International archives of occupational and environmental health

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The association between psychosocial working conditions and depressive symptoms is well established. Going beyond the association, the present study aimed to identify optimal cut-off values for psychosocial working conditions using depressive symptoms as criterion.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data from the cohort study named Study on Mental Health at Work (S-MGA) were analysed using a representative sample of employees subject to social insurance at baseline and follow-up (2011/2012, n = 4,511; 2017, n = 2,637). Psychosocial working conditions were measured at baseline using eight scales from the Copenhagen Psychosocial Questionnaire (COPSOQ), all ranging from 0 to 4, while depressive symptoms were measured at follow-up using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9; dichotomised). Cut-off values were determined by selecting the optimal combination of the corresponding sensitivity and 1 - specificity for each possible cut-off value. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves illustrate the discriminatory power of the COPSOQ scales for classifying participants as cases with or without depressive symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The analyses revealed that the optimal cut-off values for the selected COPSOQ scales ranged from 1.38 to 3.50. Area under the curve (AUC) values ranged from 0.51 (95% CI 0.47-0.54) to 0.61 (95% CI 0.57-0.64).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The method used allows to identify one optimal cut-off value on each COPSOQ scale. Due to the low discriminatory power of the COPSOQ scales for classifying individuals with depressive symptoms, the benefit of using the identified cut-off values as a classification tool is limited.

items.title: Aberrant cerebrovascular reactivity presents as an early biomarker of psychosis susceptibility in patients with 22q11.2DS.
items.authors: Delavari F, Moia S, Forrer S, Sandini C, Kojovic N, Pascucci A, Lacour C, Eliez S, Van De Ville D.

sections.text: The brain's ability to regulate blood flow is fundamental to both its function and development. In the context of neurodevelopmental disorders such as schizophrenia, understanding the complex interactions between cerebrovascular health and brain function is crucial for unraveling the pathophysiology of psychosis. This study investigates the developmental trajectory of cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) in 22q11 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) compared to healthy controls, and its association with psychosis susceptibility. Using one of the largest longitudinal data-set of resting-state fMRI, we mapped for the first time voxel-level CVR across development. We found an early reduction in CVR in 22q11.2DS, and in particular in those who later developed positive psychotic symptoms (PPS + ). These reductions were evident within the anterior cingulate cortex, frontal lobes, and globi pallidi (GP). We propose that the pattern of CVR alterations presenting early during childhood is possibly linked to altered blood-brain barrier integrity or permeability, potentially involving endothelial or tight-junction dysfunction; however, BBB integrity was not directly measured in this study. A decrease in CVR during childhood and within the frontal regions and GP was predictive of subsequent development of positive psychotic symptoms), which often occurs during adolescence in 22q11.2DS patients. These findings suggest that cerebrovascular health is critical for normal brain development, particularly in regions like the striatum, which are vulnerable to vascular damage due to their anatomical features. These results underline the potential of CVR as an early biomarker for psychosis vulnerability, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to mitigate neurodevelopmental disruptions of cerebrovascular health in 22q11.2DS.

items.title: Postmortem anterior cingulate lipid composition in people who died by suicide: exploratory multivariate findings shaped by age and environmental factors.
items.authors: Karnecki K, Mika A, Śledziński T, Steiner J, Dobrowolny H, Świerczyński J, Krzyżanowska M, Stachewicz G, Czapiewska M, Korczyńska J, Gos T.

sections.text: Suicide is a major public health concern, and lipid metabolism has been implicated in its neurobiology. We profiled fatty-acid composition in bilateral pregenual anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) samples obtained at forensic autopsy from 98 individuals (42 who died by suicide, 56 sudden-death controls) using targeted GC-MS and centered log-ratio (CLR) transformation. Analyses included exploratory univariate tests, covariate-adjusted linear mixed models (LMMs; FDR correction), and Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART) classification. Univariate tests showed nominal case-control differences in cholesterol and several n-6 PUFAs, but no lipid showed a significant main group effect after covariate-adjusted LMMs with FDR correction. Age and season were more consistent correlates of ACC lipid composition. In the full sample, a complete-case lipids-only BART model achieved CV-BCA = 72.0 ± 5.1% (n = 81; permutation p < 0.001), but interpretation was limited by different analytic samples across model types. In an adult-only sensitivity analysis (age ≥18 years; n = 92), covariate-adjusted LMMs again showed no FDR-significant group effects, whereas an exploratory mixed BART model (sex, age, PMI, ECFA 20:0, DPAn-6, EPA; n = 75 complete cases) achieved CV-BCA = 75.5 ± 3.7% and nested CV-BCA = 73.5 ± 13.3%. These findings do not support robust single-lipid suicide-associated biomarkers. Rather, they suggest that ACC lipid signals are subtle, multivariate, and strongly shaped by demographic, seasonal, and postmortem factors. The study provides a methodological caution for postmortem lipidomics and requires external validation in clinically characterized cohorts.

items.title: Screening for borderline personality disorder after self-harm episodes: validation of the self-rating KABOSS-BD, the borderline subscale of the Karolinska Affective and borderline symptoms scale.
items.authors: Asellus P, Doering S, Renberg ES, Runeson B, Waern M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is overrepresented among individuals with deliberate self-harm, yet identification of patients requiring diagnostic evaluation remains challenging in emergency settings. Effective screening tools may facilitate earlier identification of symptoms, shorten diagnostic delay, and improve treatment planning. The present study sought to validate the borderline subscale of the Karolinska Affective and Borderline Symptoms Scale (KABOSS-BD) as a self-rating screening tool for BPD in patients presenting with self-harm, and to examine its correlation with clinical diagnosis.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were analysed from 671 patients presenting with self-harm (with or without suicidal intention) at emergency departments in three Swedish cities. We investigated the internal validity of KABOSS-BD and its correlation with clinically diagnosed BPD (ICD-10 Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder) and determined optimal cut-off scores for women and men for screening purposes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The KABOSS-BD demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.87) and acceptable diagnostic accuracy in identifying patients with BPD, with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.73. The optimal cut-off score was 32, yielding sensitivity of 68% and specificity of 68%. Women consistently scored higher than men on the KABOSS-BD, and gender-specific cut-offs improved diagnostic accuracy. The scale performed optimally for women with a cut-off at 33, while for men, the scale performed better at a lower threshold of 26.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The KABOSS-BD demonstrates good internal consistency and acceptable diagnostic accuracy for BPD screening in both women and men who present with suicide attempts and non-suicidal self-harm. The scale's brevity and ease of administration make it suitable for emergency settings, potentially reducing diagnostic delay and improving treatment allocation for this high-risk population.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: Not applicable.

items.title: Migration-related factors and mental health among international students in a UK higher education setting: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Ekpenyong MS, Diba UK.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: International students may experience psychological challenges associated with migration, academic demands, and adjustment to a new cultural environment. Although previous research has documented mental health concerns in this population, less is known about the relationships among migration-related factors, perceived stress, and mental health outcomes within specific UK higher-education settings.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted among international students enrolled at the University of Wolverhampton. Data were collected using an online questionnaire that included demographic information, migration-related variables, the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21), and a measure of perceived mental stress. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise participants' characteristics and mental health outcomes. Inferential analyses included independent samples t tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson's correlation, and multiple linear regression to assess predictors of depression scores, including perceived mental stress, length of stay in the UK, gender, and region of origin.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 115 international students participated. The sample included 73 women (63.5%), 41 men (35.7%), and one participant who preferred not to report gender (0.9%). Mean scores were 1.14 (SD = 0.58) for depression, 0.98 (SD = 0.55) for anxiety, and 1.19 (SD = 0.56) for stress. Men reported higher mean depression, anxiety, and stress scores than women; however, these results should be interpreted cautiously because of the exploratory design and unequal gender groups. No statistically significant differences were identified across regions of origin, and length of stay in the UK was not significantly related to the mental health outcomes. In the regression model, perceived mental stress and gender were associated with depression scores, whereas length of stay and region of origin were not.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: In this single-institution, cross-sectional sample, perceived mental stress and gender were associated with depression scores, whereas length of stay and region of origin were not. These findings are preliminary and do not establish causality. They support the need for larger, multi-institutional, and longitudinal studies to test whether the observed relationships are reproducible and to clarify the mechanisms involved before recommending specific policy or practice changes.

items.title: Symptom severity at first digital self-assessment is not associated with greater subsequent booking of professional care on a Saudi mental health platform: a cohort study of 5,524 users.
items.authors: Alkhamees AA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Digital mental health platforms routinely deliver self-administered symptom scales on the assumption that users with more severe symptoms are more likely to enter professional care. That assumption is rarely tested with linked participant-level data, and almost never in the Arabic-speaking Gulf.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To examine whether symptom severity at a user's first self-assessment predicts booking a professional session within 90 days, across four symptom domains, on a Saudi commercial digital mental health platform.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Retrospective cohort analysis of 10,100 first assessments - depression, generalized anxiety, panic, and obsessive-compulsive scales - contributed by 5,524 unique users of the Talbinah platform and linked to demographic and session-booking records through a pseudonymous (SHA-256 hashed) user identifier. The primary outcome was any session booked within 90 days after the assessment. Severity was banded by the established cut-offs for the PHQ-9 and GAD-7, and by percentage of scale maximum for the panic and obsessive-compulsive measures, for which no severity thresholds are established. Per-scale multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR) for severity band (reference None/Minimal), adjusting for age, sex, and device type. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses used 30- and 180-day windows, an attended-session outcome, percentage-of-maximum banding applied to all four scales, and a subset with no prior booking (incident help-seeking). Reporting followed STROBE.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Users were young (mean age 26.7 years, SD 8.1) and predominantly female (78.1%); 16.6% of first assessments were followed by a booking within 90 days. No severity band on any of the four scales was associated with higher odds of booking (severe vs None/Minimal: depression aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.51-1.01; generalized anxiety 0.76, 0.49-1.16; panic 0.83, 0.52-1.31; obsessive-compulsive 1.01, 0.59-1.74). One severity contrast was statistically significant, in the opposite direction: moderate depression was associated with lower odds of booking (0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.97). Older age (aOR ~1.2 per decade) and iOS device use (1.4-2.0) were associated with booking across scales. This absence of a positive severity-booking association was consistent across 30-, 90-, and 180-day windows, the attended-session outcome, and percentage-of-maximum banding; a nominal association for moderate anxiety seen under percentage banding did not persist with validated GAD-7 cut-offs. Estimates for the panic and obsessive-compulsive scales, which lack established severity thresholds, are exploratory.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: On a Saudi digital mental health platform, greater self-reported symptom severity at first assessment was not followed by higher subsequent booking of professional care, consistently across specifications, and for moderate depression was associated with lower odds of booking; demographic and access-related attributes showed stronger associations with booking than symptom load did. Self-screening on its own appears insufficient as a pathway into care.

items.title: Psychedelic assisted psychotherapy (2020-2025): a scoping review of clinical evidence, mechanisms, safety, and ethics.
items.authors: Abdullahi NM, Menhas R, Nasir PO, Elbqry MG, Elmansy FM, Al-Ahdal SA, Alshmimry AH, Arafat AEA, Elgazzar SE, Ashmieg FSO.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Clinical research on psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT) has expanded substantially in recent years, particularly for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depressive disorders. Contemporary studies have generally evaluated psychedelic administration within controlled therapeutic settings that include psychological support, preparation, and integration. However, variability in clinical response and methodological challenges have highlighted the importance of individual, relational, and contextual factors, often described as "set and setting," in understanding therapeutic outcomes. The role of psychotherapy and the broader therapeutic context therefore remains an important area of investigation.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This scoping review aimed to map the contemporary evidence on PAT, characterize the clinical and psychotherapeutic approaches used with psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, and DMT, summarize reported clinical and safety findings, and identify methodological, mechanistic, ethical, and implementation considerations across existing protocols.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A structured search of PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted on 23 February 2026. Sources published or publicly available between January 2020 and November 2025 were eligible. The review included peer-reviewed and relevant non-peer-reviewed sources addressing psychedelic-assisted interventions, including primary clinical studies, reviews, clinical trial registrations, regulatory documents, and other relevant contextual sources. Records were managed using Zotero and screened against predefined Population, Concept, and Context criteria. Findings were synthesized descriptively according to source type and evidence domain.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The mapped evidence was most developed for MDMA-assisted therapy in PTSD and psilocybin-assisted interventions for depressive disorders. Randomized clinical trials reported reductions in PTSD and depressive symptoms following MDMA- and psilocybin-based interventions, respectively, while emerging clinical evidence also investigated LSD-based treatment for generalized anxiety disorder. Evidence for DMT-assisted therapy remained comparatively preliminary, with several available sources consisting of trial registrations or industry-reported information. Across the literature, preparation, supervised psychedelic administration, and integration were common therapeutic components, although the structure and intensity of psychotherapy varied substantially. Functional unblinding, expectancy effects, heterogeneity of psychotherapeutic approaches, and limitations in long-term safety data were recurring concerns. Ethical issues included informed consent during altered states of consciousness, therapist competence and boundaries, cultural considerations, and equitable access.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: PAT represents a rapidly developing area of clinical research, but the evidence base remains heterogeneous across compounds, indications, therapeutic models, and levels of evidential maturity. Future research should improve the standardization and reporting of psychotherapeutic interventions, strengthen methods for assessing blinding and expectancy, establish consistent long-term safety monitoring, and develop robust ethical and equity frameworks. Clear distinction between peer-reviewed clinical findings and preliminary or contextual evidence will also be essential as PAT research progresses toward broader clinical implementation.

items.title: Integrating mental health into fracture liaison services: an attribution-first policy approach to depression, concerns about falling and pathway loss.
items.authors: Liao F, Zhou F, Li X, Wang Z, Wang Q.

sections.text: Fracture liaison services (FLSs) improve delivery of secondary fracture prevention, yet eligible patients are still lost between identification, assessment, treatment recommendation, initiation, rehabilitation and follow-up. This Policy and Practice Review asks whether depression and concerns about falling should inform FLS policy, and how they could be addressed without displacing core fracture-prevention work. We synthesized structured PubMed searches with targeted appraisal of the International Osteoporosis Foundation Capture the Fracture architecture, cross-national FLS studies, clinical guidelines, audit documents and implementation-science frameworks. Evidence, derived mainly from hip-fracture populations, links depressive morbidity and mental-disorder indicators to poorer recovery or lower treatment initiation, and links concerns about falling to activity restriction and functional outcomes. These findings are prognostic rather than causal: pain, frailty, cognition, environment and service organization remain incompletely controlled. Intervention studies can improve mood or falls-related confidence without consistently improving objectively measured behavior, and no trial identified in this review used completion of an FLS engagement node as its primary outcome. Existing international and national frameworks make core FLS processes measurable, but they do not provide a consistent, auditable linkage between a non-completed node, the source of the attributed reason, the response delivered and the subsequent outcome. The England and Wales Fracture Liaison Service Database (FLS-DB) is used as a worked policy case: it records selected states such as non-attendance, patient decline and non-contactability, but its node-specific denominators and distributed fields cannot reconstruct the whole pathway. We compare four options: the status quo; cross-node reason attribution; targeted case finding linked to a named response; and a universal stepped pathway. Current evidence supports a staged sequence-attribution first, targeted measurement only where response capacity exists, and multicentre evaluation before universal standards. Evaluation should protect informed refusal, report reach and equity, preserve existing FLS performance and use prespecified stopping rules. Mental-health integration should therefore be treated as a testable quality-improvement strategy, not an established standard of care.

items.title: Depression and Anxiety in Patients with Bullous Pemphigoid: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.
items.authors: Baggus EMR, Khashkhusha A, Khashkhusha S, Butt S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is a chronic autoimmune blistering disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality. BP has previously been linked to several neurological disorders; however, its relationship with depression and anxiety remains poorly understood.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the prevalence, severity, and impact of depression and anxiety in patients with BP.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO up to August 2024. Studies involving adults (≥16 years) with BP reporting depression and/or anxiety outcomes were included. Experimental and observational peer-reviewed studies were considered. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data on mental health prevalence, effect estimates, and study quality, assessed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: This review identified a high prevalence of mental health issues in patients with BP, with depression a seemingly more consistent and pronounced issue versus anxiety. Despite this, current UK guidance provides no provision for screening and treatment of mental health issues in patients with BP. Comorbid depression was linked to increased mortality and poorer treatment adherence, suggesting a bidirectional relationship.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Integrating validated mental health screening tools such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7 in BP care is critical. A holistic approach addressing both dermatological and psychiatric aspects may improve outcomes and quality of life for BP patients.

items.title: Early self-reported medication non-adherence in depression: A hospital-based prospective study from Northeast India.
items.authors: Upadhyay A, Soohinda G, Sampath H, Dutta S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Early medication nonadherence represents a critical barrier to achieving optimal outcomes in major depressive disorder (MDD). Despite India's high depression burden, only a few studies have examined psychosocial factors associated with early nonadherence in routine clinical settings.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To evaluate the prevalence and psychosocial factors associated with early self-reported medication nonadherence in depression within 1 month of treatment in a psychiatric outpatient department.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A prospective cohort study included 101 adults diagnosed with MDD at a tertiary hospital in Northeast India who were antidepressant-naïve for the current episode and attended their first follow-up within a month. Sociodemographic and clinical factors, depression severity, and stigma were assessed at baseline. Medication adherence and medication attitudes were assessed at follow-up.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Early self-reported medication nonadherence occurred in 27.7% of patients. In bivariate analysis, nonadherence was associated with longer episode duration, treatment-emergent side effects, higher personal and perceived stigma, and poorer medication attitudes. In logistic regression, higher perceived stigma was associated with increased odds of early medication nonadherence (OR = 1.31, 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.67, P =.015) and higher drug attitude scores were associated with lower odds (OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.64 to 0.90, P <.001), whereas sociodemographic variables did not show a significant association.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Nearly one-third of MDD patients self-reported early medication nonadherence. Psychosocial determinants, particularly stigma and negative medication attitudes, played a greater role than demographic or clinical factors. Early psychoeducation and stigma-reduction strategies could be crucial for enhancing medication adherence and improving treatment outcomes in depression.

Nearly one-third of MDD patients self-reported early medication nonadherence. Psychosocial determinants, particularly stigma and negative medication attitudes, played a greater role than demographic or clinical factors. Early psychoeducation and stigma-reduction strategies could be crucial for enhancing medication adherence and improving treatment outcomes in depression.

items.title: Long-term consequences of postpartum depression on maternal psychological health and mother-child bonding: A community-based cohort study.
items.authors: Roy P, Subba SH, Parmar A, Mohanty PK, Singh AK, Behera BK, Behera P, Giri PP.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Motherhood, although perceived as a fulfilling period, is accompanied by abrupt transitions in familial and social roles, driven by physiological and psychological changes associated with hormonal fluctuations and increased caregiving responsibilities.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This study aimed to assess the long-term consequences of postpartum depression on mother-child dyads.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In the community-based cohort study, 290 postpartum mothers were followed for 6 months to 5 years. Persistent depression was assessed using the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale and confirmed by Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition diagnostic criteria. Maternal suicidality risk was measured using the Suicide Behaviours Questionnaire-Revised. Mother-child bonding was evaluated using the Mother-Infant Bonding Questionnaire. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and a P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: 29% of mothers with postpartum depression (PPD) were found to have chronic or persistent depression, and 12.9% had a high risk of suicidality. A significant association was found between PPD and persistent depression (OR = 4.74, 95% CI: 1.16-20.11, P value < 0.032). The mothers with PPD had a 16.74 times higher chance of developing increased suicidality ( P value < 0.001). Among the mothers with PPD, 69.4% had poor mother-child bonding. The mothers with PPD were found to have 4.52 times (CI: 1.80-11.31, P value 0.001) higher chance of developing poor mother-child bonding in the multivariable analysis.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Maternal PPD exerts a substantial long-term impact on both maternal psychological wellbeing and mother-child bonding. These findings underscore the need to incorporate early screening and intervention protocols for PPD within the National Mental Health Programme to mitigate long-term adverse outcomes for the mother-child dyad.

items.title: Differences in Health and Access to Care Between Heterosexual and Sexual Minority Health Care Professionals.
items.authors: Gonzales G, Connelly E, Terndrup C, Ehrenfeld JM.

sections.heading: Importance
sections.text: Little is known about the health and access to care of sexual minority health care professionals (HCPs).

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To compare health outcomes, health insurance coverage, and access to care between sexual minority and heterosexual HCPs.

sections.heading: Design, setting, and participants
sections.text: For this survey study, cross-sectional data analysis of the 2020, 2021, 2023, and 2024 National Health Interview Surveys was performed. The study population included nationally representative household probability samples of noninstitutionalized US civilian adults aged 18 years or older, restricted to HCPs working in health care settings. Data analysis was conducted between February 2024 and August 2026.

sections.heading: Exposure
sections.text: Self-reported sexual orientation, categorized as sexual minority (gay, lesbian, bisexual, or another nonheterosexual identity) or heterosexual.

sections.heading: Main outcomes and measures
sections.text: The main outcomes included cigarette smoking, lifetime diagnosis of depression, moderate to severe psychological distress, selected physical health conditions, primary source of health insurance coverage, and delayed or forgone medical care, mental health care, and prescription medications due to cost. Multivariable logistic regression models compared outcomes while adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The sample included 2890 HCPs (2731 heterosexual and 159 sexual minority; mean [SE] age, 44.9 [0.7] years; 74.7% [0.9%] female [survey weighted]). Sexual minority individuals represented 5.7% (95% CI, 4.8%-6.7%) of HCPs and were more likely to be younger (aged 26-34 years: 38.8% [95% CI, 30.1%-48.3%] vs 24.0% [95% CI, 22.2%-25.9%]), never married (32.7% [95% CI, 24.7%-41.8%] vs 14.6% [95% CI, 13.0%-16.4%]), and living in households below the federal poverty level (7.4% [95% CI, 3.4%-15.4%] vs 1.1% [95% CI, 0.7%-1.7%]) compared with heterosexual HCPs. Sexual minority HCPs were significantly more likely to report a lifetime diagnosis of depression (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 3.05 [95% CI, 2.02-4.59]), moderate to severe psychological distress (AOR, 2.06 [95% CI, 1.23-3.46]), arthritis (AOR, 2.45 [95% CI, 1.42-4.22]), and delayed medical care due to cost (AOR, 2.06 [95% CI, 1.14-3.72]). Sexual minority HCPs faced greater disparities in access to care: they were more likely to forgo mental health care (AOR, 3.74 [95% CI, 2.11-6.63]) and to forgo prescription medications (AOR, 4.81 [95% CI, 2.52-9.15]) due to cost than their heterosexual peers.

sections.heading: Conclusions and relevance
sections.text: In this cross-sectional survey study of HCPs, sexual minority HCPs were more likely than heterosexual HCPs to report depression, psychological distress, and financial barriers to health care. These findings highlight disparities in health and access to care among sexual minority HCPs and the need for workplace supports to address factors contributing to these disparities.

items.title: Effects of direct cannabinoid receptor modulation on alcohol craving and withdrawal: a systematic review.
items.authors: Archey Drennan ML, Hetelekides EM, Karoly HC.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a prevalent condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality rates. Existing pharmacological and psychosocial treatments offer limited long-term effectiveness. At present, there is a critical need for novel AUD treatments. The endogenous cannabinoid system (ECS) may offer some therapeutic promise for AUD, given that it appears to play a role in alcohol use motivation, while alcohol alters ECS function. Since craving and withdrawal are key AUD symptoms and represent important treatment targets, the role of the ECS in mediating craving and withdrawal should be fully explored. Exploitation of the ECS may have potential as a treatment target for AUD.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This review synthesizes results from preclinical investigations into the impact of cannabinoid (CB) receptor modulation on measures of craving and withdrawal since the discovery of the CB1 receptor.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Researchers identified studies published between 1988 and 2026 involving direct CB receptor modulation, measuring outcomes pertaining to craving or withdrawal, and containing a control group were included in qualitative synthesis. Studies focused on alcohol consumption were not analyzed unless craving or withdrawal-related outcomes were reported. Risk of bias was examined using the SYRCLE tool for preclinical studies.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Thirty-nine studies met inclusion criteria, all preclinical. Overall, CB1 activation generally increases craving-related behaviors, while antagonism tends to attenuate craving and some withdrawal-related outcomes, although dose-dependent effects were also reported. CB2 may mediate reinforcing effects of alcohol, but direction of effects is inconsistent. Evidence regarding withdrawal is limited and inconsistent.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Preclinical evidence suggests that cannabinoid receptor modulation influences alcohol craving and withdrawal-related behaviors. Integration of these behavioral findings with the broader ECS literature suggests that CB1-mediated reward and motivational processes, and CB2-mediated neuroimmune signaling may represent important mechanisms underlying these phenotypes. Greater methodological standardization and clinical investigation are needed to confirm these mechanisms and determine their translational potential for AUD treatment.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: The protocol was pre-registered through Prospero (registration CRD42022309872) on 5/31/22.

items.title: Postoperative complications from alcohol use disorder in an adult congenital heart disease patient: a case report emphasizing the role of high-complexity congenital centers.
items.authors: Alexander B, Greiten L, Sanders E.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Superior sinus venous atrial septal defect (SVASD) associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) is a rare congenital heart disease that is predominantly diagnosed and surgically treated in childhood; however, sometimes the diagnosis is delayed and requires intervention in adulthood.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: A 69-year-old patient presented to the adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) clinic due to shortness of breath and recurrent syncopal episodes and was found to have significant right ventricular enlargement by echocardiogram of undetermined cause. Cardiac CT detected a large SVASD with PAPVR that required surgical intervention. The postoperative course was complicated by delirium tremens.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: ACHD patients often have many comorbidities that are not commonly seen in the pediatric population. Because of this, it is of utmost importance that pediatric surgical centers offering procedures for ACHD patients have established protocols to manage these comorbidities postoperatively, including substance withdrawal symptoms.

items.title: Balancing Urgency and Care: Discursive Perspectives on Anxiety-Related School Refusal in Adolescents-Institutional, Nursing, and Transcultural Insights From a French Maison des Adolescents.
items.authors: Radjack R, Rizzi AT, Massari N, Brown D, Harf A, Mazeaud E, Baveux C, Moro MR.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety-related school refusal is a complex phenomenon that raises questions at the intersection of psychiatry, education, and family systems.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: This perspective article examines therapeutic and institutional approaches developed in a French Maison des Adolescents, a specialised multidisciplinary centre for adolescent mental health. We discuss the tensions between urgency expressed by families and schools, and the need for a graded reintegration whose timing is set by the adolescent's clinical condition.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: Clinical vignettes illustrate the overlap between school refusal, comorbid psychiatric symptoms, and sociocultural factors, including migration and trauma.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We argue that care must be conceived on three interconnected levels: individual, family, and environmental. Options such as weekly day hospital programmes, multifamily therapy, and transcultural consultations demonstrate both strengths and limitations.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: For and against arguments are highlighted: while institutional programmes provide containment and support, they may also risk premature or excessive intervention.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The central question addressed is: How can multidisciplinary adolescent care centres best support young people with anxiety-related school refusal while balancing urgency, family dynamics, and educational reintegration?

sections.heading: Implications for nursing practice
sections.text: First-contact nursing assessment combines relational engagement, physical and mental-health assessment, and risk identification to guide timely referral and an agreed care plan. Nurses engage adolescents and families, help contain pressure for immediate school return, and contribute to care coordination and collaborative, graded school reintegration adjusted to the adolescent's clinical condition. Ultimately, anxiety-related school refusal must be approached as a systemic issue requiring joint solutions from health, education, and family contexts. Our reflections aim to inform international practice and stimulate debate on therapeutic, institutional, and transcultural options for managing this condition.

items.title: From suicidal ideation to hope: Perceived mental health transformation following a culturally adapted multiple family group therapy for adolescents living with HIV in Ghana - A qualitative process evaluation.
items.authors: Boakye DS, Deegbe DA, Dzansi G, Anum A, Adjorlolo S.

sections.text: Adolescents living with HIV (ALHIV) in sub-Saharan Africa experience profound mental health challenges including depression, anxiety, and suicidal ideation. Evidence-based psychological interventions specifically designed for this population remain scarce, particularly family-based approaches in resource-limited settingsThis study explored ALHIV's perceived mental health transformation following participation in culturally adapted Multiple Family Group Therapy (MFGT) in Ghana.Qualitative study nested within a randomized controlled trial (NCT06701942) conducted in Lower Manya Krobo District, Ghana. Nineteen ALHIV who completed the 10-MFGT core content sessions. MFGT intervention participated in three focus group discussions. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis.Three major themes emerged: (1) Pre-Intervention Mental Health Crisis, (2) Psychological Change Mechanisms, and (3) Mental Health Transformation. Pre-intervention, ALHIV described experiencing profound mental health crisis-level distress including active suicidal ideation with method-specific planning, emotional dysregulation, and existential foreclosure. Intervention mechanisms facilitating transformation included cognitive reframing through culturally resonant metaphors, dual-level universality (peer and intergenerational family), biomedical knowledge (U = U) as psychological intervention, and emotional catharsis in safe spaces. Post-intervention, participants described substantial perceived improvements in mental health characterized by reduced suicidal ideation, emotional regulation gains, reduced anxiety, and greater psychological peace.Culturally adapted family-based group therapy was associated with meaningful mental health improvements, including reduced suicidal ideation. Participants described shifts in emotional wellbeing, coping, and family cohesion, though the qualitative design precludes causal claims. Findings support the feasibility of task-shifted, family-centered interventions in resource-limited settings and underscore the need to integrate mental health screening and family-based support into HIV diagnosis protocols. Trial registration Clinical trials.gov (NCT06701942).

items.title: Changes in self-related cognitive processes and depressive symptom severity following a single, moderate dose of psilocybin in depressed patients.
items.authors: Belinger L, Moujaes F, von Rotz R, Rieser NM, Funk X, Egger K, Meinhold L, Renkert M, Stämpfli P, Herdener M, Vollenweider FX, Preller KH.
items.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
items.journal_abbrev: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci

sections.text: Psychedelic-assisted therapy, particularly with psilocybin, is increasingly proposed as a treatment for major depressive disorder, yet the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying its effects remain under investigation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, individuals diagnosed with major depressive disorder received a single, moderate dose of psilocybin (0.215 mg kg-1) or placebo, with the same psychological support. We analysed N = 37 individuals with major depressive disorder undergoing assessments of depressive symptoms (Beck's depression inventory and Montgomery-Åsberg depression rating scale), self-concept (Frankfurt self-concept scale) and neural markers of self-referential processing using an fMRI-based task. Compared with placebo, the psilocybin group exhibited significant reductions in depressive symptoms and a significant increase in positive self-concept two weeks after substance administration. Changes in self-concept were significantly correlated with decreased depressive scores. Neuroimaging revealed psilocybin-associated modulation of caudate activation during externally oriented attention after two weeks, contrasting with placebo-induced caudate changes during self-referential processing. These findings extend prior evidence linking psychedelics to changes in self-referential processing and self-concept and demonstrate that such changes occur concurrently with reductions in depressive symptoms. Future research should aim to replicate and extend these results and refine therapy protocols targeting self-processing and self-concept in psychedelic-assisted therapy in major depressive disorder. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

items.title: Conceptualizing the process of experiential acceptance during an episode of anxiety: A qualitative study of individuals with prior experience in mindfulness- and acceptance-based interventions.
items.authors: Ribeyron J, Duriez N, Shankland R.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Experiential acceptance refers to the capacity to be open to internal experiences without attempting to change or avoid them. Although acceptance is a core emotion regulation strategy within mindfulness- and acceptance-based interventions (MABIs) and a protective factor for mental health, its conceptualization and implementation remain unclear and ambiguous. The aim of this study was to clarify and develop a model of accepting anxiety as experienced by individuals with prior experience in MABIs.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Twenty-six participants from a non-clinical sample with varying levels of prior experience in MABIs took part in semi-structured interviews exploring their experience of accepting anxiety. Data collection and analysis followed the principles of Grounded Theory to generate a data-driven model of the acceptance process.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: We identified a five-stage dynamic model involving distinct processes: observing through the body with attentional focus on interoceptive experience; identifying and acknowledging anxiety; validating and normalizing the experience through validation and self-compassion; observing from an observer stance characterized by decentering; and maintaining flexible contact with the experience via interoceptive exposure and nonreactivity. We also identified facilitating factors that support engagement in the acceptance process.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings refine the understanding of acceptance as a multidimensional emotion regulation process by highlighting an active dynamic involving multiple mechanisms underlying the acceptance of anxiety. As experienced by individuals with prior MABI experience, this model provides a framework for developing more targeted clinical interventions and for investigating individual and contextual variability in these subprocesses.

items.title: The Impact of Financial Toxicity on Mental Health of LGBTQ+ Cancer Caregivers in the United States.
items.authors: Tan KR, Murray CR, Jones SR, Warner EL, Black M, Belcher S, Charlton BM, Coombs LA, Donovan HS, Fredrickson BL, Kent EE, Nichols HB, Zhang H, Waters AR.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Financial toxicity and poor mental health are common among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and other non-cisgender heterosexual (LGBTQ+) cancer caregivers. This study aimed to assess the relationship between financial toxicity and mental health among LGBTQ+cancer caregivers.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study (national survey and semi-structured interviews with a subset of survey participants). Data were collected from April 2024 through December 2024. Bivariate and multivariable regression models were used to examine the association between financial toxicity (modified COmprehensive Score for financial Toxicity [mCOST]) and mental health outcomes (Mental Health Continuum-SF [MHC-SF] and Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System [PROMIS] domains of anxiety, depression, sleep disturbance, and fatigue).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of N = 316 LGBTQ+cancer caregivers participated in the survey, and N = 14 participated in an interview. Among caregivers, 34.5% reported high financial toxicity (mCOST< 22). The average MHC-SF score was 38.4 (SD: 16.9, range: 0-70). Mean PROMIS domain T-scores were: anxiety 59.7 (SD: 10.0, range: 40.3-81.6), depression 56.2 (SD: 10.6, range: 41.0-79.4), sleep disturbance 54.2 (SD: 9.2, range: 32-73.3), and fatigue 54.8 (SD: 11.9, range: 33.7-75.8). In controlled multivariable models, high financial toxicity was significantly associated with poorer mental health (lower MHC-SF scores [beta = -10.56, 95% CI: -14.47 to -6.65], and higher PROMIS anxiety [beta = 8.54, 95% CI: 6.33-10.74], depression [beta = 7.49, 95% CI: 5.07-9.91], sleep disturbance [beta = 6.33, 95% CI: 4.16-8.50], and fatigue [beta = 8.94, 95% CI: 6.26-11.63]. Qualitative analysis yielded two themes: (1) Financial Stress and Frustration and (2) Negative impacts of financial toxicity on health.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: LGBTQ+cancer caregivers experience high financial toxicity that is associated with poor mental health outcomes. Financial toxicity should be addressed in addition to general caregiving-related stress in this at-risk population.

items.title: N-Acetylcysteine-Induced Hepatotoxicity and Urticaria in a 9-Year-Old Girl.
items.authors: El-Qurneh O, Suhasini M.

sections.text: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is increasingly used off-label in pediatric populations to manage psychiatric disorders, particularly repetitive behaviors and anxiety-related conditions. Although generally considered safe, rare but serious adverse reactions, including hepatotoxicity, have been reported. This report describes a 9-year-old girl with anxiety and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder who developed severe transaminitis and urticaria following NAC therapy prescribed for skin-picking behavior. The patient presented with peak alanine aminotransferase of 1,417 U/L and aspartate aminotransferase of 541 U/L and a diffuse urticarial rash that developed 5 days after NAC initiation. Complete resolution occurred within 3 weeks of discontinuing NAC. This case highlights the potential for serious hepatotoxicity associated with NAC in pediatric patients, emphasizing the importance of baseline liver function monitoring and education regarding early signs of adverse reactions when using NAC off-label for psychiatric indications.

items.title: German medical students' learning environment during the fading COVID-19 pandemic.
items.authors: Leich M, Guse J, Bergelt C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The Medical School's learning environment (MSLE) is important for medical students' academic performance and mental well-being. COVID-19 disrupted medical education worldwide through restrictions on practical and in-person teaching. Although several studies have showcased the immediate effects on medical students' perceptions of MSLE and mental well-being, less is known about the changes during the transition to post-pandemic medical education.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Four cross-sectional online surveys were conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Various validated items assessed distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Across four survey waves, 687 individual medical and dental students participated. Positive MSLE perceptions were more frequent in later waves, although differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Social connectedness and access to mentoring were reported significantly more frequently in later waves. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with lower odds of positive MSLE. The proportion reporting decreased study motivation since the onset of COVID-19 was significantly lower in the final wave. Older students, those in more advanced study years, and those experiencing loneliness or distress more frequently reported decreased motivation. Mental burden showed varying patterns: loneliness was generally lower in later waves, distress peaked in summer 2022, depressive symptoms and perceived stress in winter 2022/2023, and anxiety in summer 2023. After correction for multiple comparisons, only differences in distress across survey waves remained significant. Female students reported higher anxiety, loneliness, and perceived stress than male students, but only the gender difference in anxiety remained significant after correction.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Medical students reported a more positive perception of the MSLE in later survey waves during the transition from pandemic to post-pandemic medical education. However, these improvements were not matched by a uniform recovery in medical students' well-being. Medical schools are therefore encouraged to strengthen students' learning environments by ensuring learning opportunities, mentoring, and mental health support throughout training.
