items.title: Assessing the psychometric properties of the Symptom Checklist Five-Items (SCL-5) instrument in a clinical setting for treating intimate partner violence.
items.authors: Nesset MB, Palmstierna T, Whittington R, Lara-Cabrera ML.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Research suggests that the Symptom Checklist Five Items (SCL-5) instrument is a reliable and valid scale for assessing mental health in a range of populations. Yet, to date, the SCL-5 has not been validated in a population of perpetrators of intimate partner violence (IPV) and their partners. Hence, the current study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the SCL-5 within a clinical IPV context characterized by elevated mental health symptoms.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This validation study is part of a randomised controlled trial evaluating a group intervention for men voluntarily seeking treatment for IPV in Norway. The study was conducted in accordance with the guidelines Consensus-based standards for the selection of health measurement instruments (COSMIN). We evaluated floor and ceiling effects, internal consistency and estimated the area under the curve to determine optimal diagnostic sensitivity and specificity. Additionally, we explored scale responsiveness using data from a subsample of participants.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The highest percentage of respondents with the lowest possible score (value 1) across the 5 items was 8.7%, indicating no floor effect assuming the 15% criterion. The highest percentage with the highest possible score (value 4) across the 5 items was 1.9%, indicating no ceiling effect either. Cronbach's alpha was 0.86 for the total sample (N = 161), 0.83 for perpetrators only (n = 118) and 0.89 for partners only (n = 44). The area under the curve was 94.6% (95% CI 0.913-0.978) for the total sample, 93.5% (95% CI 0.893-0.977) for the perpetrators and 96.9% (95% CI 0.922-1.017) for the victims. Regarding responsiveness, we set a criterion of a statistically significant reduction in mean scores over time as a test of the adequate responsiveness of the SCL-5 from the baseline to the one-year follow-up point. As predicted, it fell from 1.98 to 1.74 and the mean change was significant (t -4.021, CI -0.360 to -0.121; p < 0.001). The mean total SCL-5 score decreased in 54% of cases (n = 43).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The results provide evidence that the SCL-5 has adequate psychometric properties in a Norwegian sample of perpetrators and victims of IPV.

sections.heading: Clinical trial number
sections.text: Not applicable.

items.title: Temporal interference stimulation for working memory deficits in schizophrenia: a pilot trial.
items.authors: Zhang Z, Chi J, Wang Q, Han Y, Hou W, Zhou J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Working memory impairment represents a core domain of cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia. Temporal interference stimulation (TIs) is a novel neuromodulation approach that enables focal and noninvasive stimulation across cortical and subcortical regions. This study was performed to assess the feasibility, safety, and working memory changes associated with TIs in schizophrenia.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This single-arm trial enrolled 20 patients with schizophrenia and working memory impairment from March to April 2025. TIs targeting the posterior parietal cortex was administered twice daily for five consecutive days. Clinical and cognitive assessments were conducted at baseline, week 1, and week 2. The primary outcome was the change in spatial span test score from baseline to week 1. Secondary outcomes included week-2 change in the spatial span test score, changes in the delay-estimation task and continuous performance test (CPT), and changes in clinical symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Twenty patients completed the trial. Spatial span test scores were significantly higher at week 1 than at baseline, and statistically significant increases from baseline were also observed at week 2 in the spatial span test and CPT. No significant correlations were found between cognitive changes and clinical changes. Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated significant increases in spatial span test performance at weeks 1 and 2 among patients in the clinically impaired subgroup, but not among those in the mildly impaired subgroup. No serious adverse events were reported.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This trial offers preliminary evidence that TIs is safe and well-tolerated in schizophrenia and is associated with dissociable cognitive increases, particularly among those with clinically significant cognitive impairment at baseline.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: The trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500098361) on March 6, 2025.

items.title: Demographic and psychosocial factors associated with adjustment and reintegration to civilian life: a prospective and cross-sectional analysis of transitioning and ex-serving military personnel.
items.authors: Romaniuk M, Fisher G, Batterham PJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The prevalence of reintegration and adjustment difficulties among military veterans transitioning to civilian life is high, with maladjustment linked to poor mental health and increased suicide risk. Identifying factors predictive of adjustment may inform the development of preventative screening and intervention strategies. This study aimed to determine significant demographic and psychosocial factors associated with adjustment and reintegration using both cross-sectional and prospective methods.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A convenience sample of 866 transitioning and ex-serving military personnel completed demographic, service, and psychosocial questionnaires online. A subset provided responses before and after permanent separation from service. Binary logistic regression analyses were used to assess the association between key variables and self-reported adjustment and reintegration to civilian life. The effects of the predictor variables on the outcome variable were estimated by adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: For ex-serving participants, significant associations were found between adjustment/reintegration and gender (p =.045), education level (p =.031), marital status (p = .022), rank at discharge (p < .001), employment status (p < .001), number of years since discharge (p = .001), PTSD symptoms (p < .001), purpose and connection (p < .001), help seeking (p = .019), and beliefs about civilians (p < .001). For current serving participants, significant associations included employment status (p < .001) anger and perceived failure (p =.02) and feeling unprepared for civilian life (p = .002).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Veterans at higher risk of maladjustment include those who are unemployed or on a medical pension, are single, male, from lower ranks with lower education, and with higher symptoms of PTSD, higher levels of anger, feelings of failure, and feeling unprepared for the transition to civilian life prior to separation. Embedding population-level monitoring of this high-risk demographic group, along with individual-level screening and targeting of these factors may assist in improving adjustment and reintegration outcomes in this population.

items.title: Plasma Metabolome Mediates the Link Between Chronic Pain and Brain Disorders: A Large-Scale Cohort and Genetic Analysis.
items.authors: Pan L, Yang W, Chen Z, Chen L, Sun K, Liu Y, Ding W, Wang X, Chen H, Mou Y, Chen Y, Zhong S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Chronic pain has been linked to neurological and psychiatric disorders, yet the metabolic mechanisms driving this association remain unclear.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Leveraging data from 174,630 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations of 251 plasma metabolites with chronic pain across seven body sites and constructed a metabolic signature using elastic net regression. Cox proportional hazards models were applied to explore the associations of chronic pain and the metabolic signature with 10 incident brain disorders. For outcomes with significant associations, we evaluated genetic causality of the identified metabolites using Mendelian randomization (MR). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate inflammatory pathways involving eight markers, such as platelet count and C-reactive protein.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Most metabolites were significantly associated with chronic pain (FDR-corrected p < 0.05), with 88 metabolites forming a metabolic signature. During a median follow-up of 15.6 years, an increasing number of chronic pain sites and a higher metabolic signature were associated with increased risks of depression, anxiety, and ischemic stroke (IS). Systemic inflammation, particularly platelet and leukocyte counts, partially mediated the effect of the metabolic signature on depression (4.33%) and IS (9.52%). Furthermore, MR analyses suggested potential causal roles for several metabolites in these outcomes, such as docosahexaenoic acid (DHA).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Our findings highlight the pivotal role of metabolic dysregulation in the connection between chronic pain and brain disorders. These results offer valuable insights into inflammation-mediated mechanisms and identify potential metabolic biomarkers for prevention.

items.title: Longitudinal trajectories of non-suicidal self-injury, suicidal ideation, and suicide attempts following standardized outpatient emergency management in adolescents.
items.authors: Jarvers I, Ecker A, Schleicher D, Otto A, Brunner R, Kandsperger S.
items.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Emergency presentations for non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), suicidal ideation, and suicide attempts in youth have increased markedly. Behavioural and ideational components of self-injury and suicidality may follow partially dissociable courses, underscoring the need for longitudinal evaluation after emergency care.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To examine longitudinal changes in NSSI behaviour, NSSI thoughts, suicidal ideation, and suicide attempts after standardized outpatient emergency management; identify psychological and familial predictors; and assess the perceived benefit of safety planning.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants were 105 adolescents (mean age = 14.9 years) presenting in acute crisis to an outpatient emergency service with NSSI and/or suicidal ideation/suicide attempt, followed up twice. Measures included NSSI and suicidal thoughts and behaviour, emotional reactivity, psychological distress, patient and parental motivation, parental stress, and perceived benefit of the safety plan. Changes over time were analysed using non-parametric tests of both frequency and prevalence, and predictors using linear mixed-effects models.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Changes differed by dimension: suicide attempts declined in both frequency and prevalence, NSSI behaviour declined in frequency, and NSSI thoughts and suicidal ideation in prevalence while overall frequency was unchanged. Emotional reactivity, general psychological distress, and patient motivation improved. Higher patient motivation was independently associated with lower NSSI behaviour over time, while no variables significantly predicted NSSI thoughts. Parental, but not adolescent, perceived benefit of the safety plan was associated with reduced NSSI behaviour at follow-up.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Following emergency management, self-injurious behaviour and ideation followed partially dissociable courses. Behavioural improvement was linked to adolescent motivation and parental engagement, whereas ideation improved less completely: fewer adolescents reported suicidal or NSSI-related thoughts, but their frequency did not decline. Ideation therefore warrants continued, targeted monitoring even when behaviour improves.

items.title: Exploring Barriers to Accessing Mental Health Services for Adolescents With Depression in Pokhara Metropolitan City, Nepal: Perspectives of Mental Healthcare Providers.
items.authors: Thompson M, Cardno A, Joshi D.

sections.text: Background In Nepal, depression is one of the most common mental health conditions among adolescents, but mental health services for this population remain limited. Previous studies have identified barriers to accessing mental health services in Nepal; however, to our knowledge, no study has specifically examined the barriers faced by adolescents with depression. Aims This study aimed to identify barriers to accessing mental health services for adolescents with depression in Pokhara Metropolitan City, Nepal, from the perspectives of mental healthcare providers, and to identify approaches to overcome these barriers. Method Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine healthcare professionals involved in delivering mental healthcare, including counsellors, psychologists, medical officers, and consultant psychiatrists. Participants were selected through purposive sampling according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Interviews were conducted in May 2023 at the participants' workplaces across Pokhara Metropolitan City. The interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to develop codes and themes. Results Barriers to accessing mental health services included individual factors, primarily related to limited knowledge of mental health and available services; social factors, including stigma, particularly within families and the wider community; and systemic and structural factors, including limited service availability and an insufficient mental health workforce. Suggested strategies to overcome these barriers included raising mental health awareness in schools and through social media, as well as increasing the number of mental health-trained staff providing services within communities. Conclusions Recommendations for future practice include integrating mental health education into Nepal's national school curriculum and expanding training programs for healthcare workers. Future research could explore perspectives from other regions of Nepal and include additional stakeholder groups, such as adolescents, parents of adolescents, and government staff.

items.title: Motivational Strategies in Digital Interventions for Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD): A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Ali N, Shreedhar S, Oconnell P, Lambert L.

sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with impairments in executive functioning and difficulties sustaining attention and goal-directed behaviour. Digital interventions offer a promising avenue for addressing these difficulties because they can modulate task demands and deliver immediate reinforcement, although evidence for their superiority over conventional interventions remains limited. This scoping review mapped the motivational strategies, defined as discrete intervention features intended to encourage engagement, participation, persistence, or responsiveness, distinct from the underlying cognitive training itself, incorporated into digital interventions targeting executive functioning and ADHD-related outcomes in children aged 6-12 years. Six studies published between 2018 and 2026, identified through a PubMed search, met the inclusion criteria. Five were randomized controlled trials, and one was a pilot study. All six studies reported immediate feedback, five reported adaptive difficulty, four reported points or scores, and three reported in-game rewards and progress tracking. Each of virtual currency, narrative, customization, and explicit positive reinforcement was reported in one of six studies. Competitive leaderboards were reported in none. Although all six studies reported improvement in at least one outcome, heterogeneity in intervention design and outcome assessment, together with the very limited evidence base and the single-database search, precluded attribution of these findings to specific motivational strategies. It remains a hypothesis, rather than an established finding, that motivational design may influence how children interpret performance, regulate effort, and persist when faced with cognitive demand. Future research should examine motivational strategies as distinct components of intervention design and determine whether particular strategies are associated with sustained engagement and improvements in executive functioning or ADHD-related outcomes.

items.title: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder as a Potential Early-Life Risk Factor for Dementia: A Life-Course Perspective.
items.authors: Park SH.

sections.text: Current models of modifiable dementia risk span the life course but begin with formal education, leaving the prenatal period unexamined. Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) is the leading preventable cause of neurodevelopmental disability; its clinical expression is fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD), of which fetal alcohol syndrome is the most severe form. FASD affects about 0.8% of children worldwide and considerably more in residential and foster care, yet its late-life trajectory is unstudied: the first diagnosed cohort is only now in its sixth decade. This review examines whether PAE may be an early-life dementia risk factor. In rodent models, developmental alcohol exposure produces hippocampal, cholinergic, and epigenetic changes demonstrable in adult animals; the report of Alzheimer-type markers in middle-aged exposed animals rests on a single unreplicated study. In humans, FASD is associated with low cognitive reserve, social adversity, and a high prevalence of adult alcohol use disorder, each an established dementia risk factor. Two hypotheses are distinguished: a pathology hypothesis, in which PAE promotes neurodegenerative change, and a reserve hypothesis, in which lower premorbid reserve brings forward clinical expression at comparable pathological burden. The expected phenotype is more likely mixed than purely Alzheimer-type. No human evidence yet links PAE to incident dementia; the proposition remains a hypothesis, not an established association. Given the mechanistic plausibility, examination is warranted through midlife biomarker studies and record linkage in cohorts with documented exposure; recording PAE in memory clinic history taking and at entry into residential and foster care would supply the data required.

items.title: Prevalence and determinants of fatal self immolation among hospitalized burn patients in Northern Iran during an ElevenYears study.
items.authors: Ghorbani M, MohsenimoallemKolaei N, Hesamirostami M, Najafikersami S, Shokrizadeharani L, Hosseinnattaj A, Ghasemiateni F, Arabkhazaeli N, Elyasi F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Fatal selfimmolation is a severe form of intentional burn injury with high mortality and a substantial psychosocial burden. However, limited evidence exists regarding its longterm epidemiological trends and associated factors among hospitalized burn patients in northern Iran. This study aimed to investigate the frequency, temporal trend, and determinants of fatal selfimmolation among deceased burn patients in a hospital in Northern Iran over 11 years.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: This retrospective study included all burnrelated deaths recorded in a referral burn center in northern Iran from March 2011 to March 2022. The study was conducted in a university- affiliated burn hospital located in Mazandaran province, which also serves as a referral center for patients from other cities. Data was collected and analyzed to assess the prevalence of selfimmolation and its associated factors. Descriptive statistics and logistic regression were performed using SPSS version 21 to examine factors associated with fatal selfimmolation. Chi-square test and multivariate logistic regression were applied; Variables with p < 0.3 in univariate analysis were entered into the final model, and model adequacy was assessed. This study reflects the proportion of selfimmolation only among fatal burn cases and does not include surviving patients; therefore, results should be interpreted within the context of a hospital based mortality cohort.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among all burn cases during the study period, 882 patients (10.65%) died The burn cause was not recorded in 203 (23%) of deceased patients. Of the 679 deceased patients with available data, 117 (17.2%) had committed selfimmolation. Among deceased patients, 399 cases (58.8%) were men, 340 (50.1%) were aged 41-60 years, 433 (63.8%) were married, and 249 (36.7%) were employed. Women had higher odds of fatal selfimmolation compared with men (OR = 2.56). Single individuals had 3.05 times higher odds of fatal self-immolation compared with married individuals. Patients from Golestan province and other provinces had 1.72 and 3.26 times higher odds, respectively, compared with those residing in Mazandaran province. Furthermore, individuals with a history of psychiatric treatment had 4.85 times higher odds of fatal selfimmolation.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Fatal selfimmolation showed an increasing trend after 2018. It was independently associated with female sex, single marital status, residence outside Mazandaran province, and a history of psychiatric treatment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a hospital-based fatal burn cohort and do not reflect incidence in the general population These results highlight the need for targeted mental health interventions and region specific preventive strategies.

items.title: Associations between prenatal heatwave exposure and child development and behavior and the mediating role of maternal depression in Brazil.
items.authors: Kawaoka Komatsu B, Martins Linhares MB, Menezes-Filho N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense under climate change. Although prenatal heat exposure has been linked to adverse birth outcomes, its implications for early-childhood development and behavior remain poorly understood in tropical low- and middle-income settings. We examined whether prenatal heatwave exposure is associated with infant development and behavior, and whether current maternal depression mediates this association.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We used data from the Brazilian Center for Early Child Development (CPAPI) birth cohort in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, Brazil, comprising 946 infants born between July 2023 and March 2024. We assessed development and behavior at 6-10 months using the Survey of Well-being of Young Children and derived prenatal heatwave exposure from climate reanalysis data linked to maternal residential addresses. We estimated associations using a high-dimensional fixed-effects framework, adjusting for family, infant, and neighborhood characteristics, historical climate, and postnatal climate exposure, and decomposed these associations using a mediation analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Prenatal heatwave exposure was not associated with developmental milestone scores. However, each additional heatwave day during pregnancy was associated with higher infant irritability, with a risk increase of approximately 13%. Prenatal exposure was also associated with increased maternal depressive symptoms, which accounted for 21%-22% of the associations with behavioral outcomes.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Prenatal heatwave exposure was associated with early behavioral difficulties, suggesting that early behavioral regulation may be particularly sensitive to prenatal heat. Maternal mental health appears to be an important pathway, highlighting its relevance for climate adaptation and early-childhood health strategies.

items.title: Trajectories of mental health and well-being across healthcare workers during COVID-19 pandemic: a Swiss longitudinal study.
items.authors: Bhatia C, Moullec G, Corbaz-Kurth S, Vieux L, Wozniak H, Roos P, Suard JC, Benzakour L, Cereghetti S, Weissbrodt R, Pralong JA.

sections.text: This longitudinal study examined the trajectories of healthcare workers' mental health from the first to the second COVID-19 wave (May 2020-December 2020) in a Swiss tertiary hospital, and their association with individual and organizational factors. For each mental health outcome (depression, anxiety, peritraumatic stress, and well-being), a separate analysis identified two trajectories: one with higher, persistent levels of symptoms and one that was resilient, with low-level symptoms. The persistent trajectory comprised about 25%-30% of participants for anxiety, depression and peritraumatic stress and 47% for well-being; because the classifications were outcome-specific, membership differed across outcomes (about 15% of participants were on a persistent trajectory for all four outcomes and 46% resilient for all four). We found that women, nurses, caregivers, non-managerial employees, and frontline COVID-19 workers were more likely to follow a persistent trajectory. Organizational risk factors were a high workload and an irregular work schedule. These results provide a basis for implementing risk-adapted prevention measures and resilience-promotion programs to protect health workers from the impact of major crises. Future research should address the needs of vulnerable health workers to provide evidence-based health promotion.

items.title: Case Report: Severe depression and suicidality in a young patient with RYR1-related congenital myopathy.
items.authors: Radu ŞA, Vasiliu O, Tudor C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: RYR1-related congenital myopathies (RYR1-CMYO) are rare inherited neuromuscular disorders characterized by considerable clinical and histopathological heterogeneity. Although chronic physical disability may be associated with substantial psychological burden, psychiatric manifestations in patients diagnosed with RYR1-related disorders remain insufficiently characterized.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: We report the case of an 18-year-old man with a longstanding RYR1-related congenital myopathy with an autosomal dominant family pattern, who was admitted for a severe depressive episode with active suicidal ideation and a suicide plan. The patient also met diagnostic criteria for obsessive-compulsive disorder and retrospectively reported psychotic symptoms of uncertain timing, duration, and diagnostic significance. No active psychotic symptoms were identified at the documented examination. The familial RYR1 p.Leu4579Arg missense variant had previously been identified in both the patient and his clinically affected mother, supporting segregation with the neuromuscular phenotype. However, patient-specific muscle histopathology was unavailable. A particularly salient psychosocial feature was marked resentment toward his mother, whom he perceived as responsible for transmitting the disorder, in the context of longstanding physical disability, reduced autonomy, and intrafamilial conflict. An individualized multimodal treatment approach combining pharmacotherapy, described family-oriented work, suicide-risk management, and multidisciplinary follow-up was associated with partial improvement in depressive symptoms and reduction of active suicidal ideation during follow-up. The contributions of individual interventions could not be separated.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This case illustrates the psychiatric and psychosocial burden of living with an inherited disabling neuromuscular disease in a young adult. Although a direct pathophysiological relationship between RYR1 dysfunction and major depressive disorder or an RYR1-specific psychiatric phenotype cannot be inferred, chronic disability, impaired autonomy, awareness of genetic transmission, and associated family dynamics may contribute to psychological distress. The case highlights the importance of systematic assessment of depression and suicide risk in patients with rare disabling neuromuscular disorders and supports the integration of psychiatric care, psychological support, genetic counseling, and family-oriented interventions within multidisciplinary management.

items.title: Correlation between hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal function and clinical characteristics in the acute phase of first-episode drug-naive major depressive disorder.
items.authors: Liu L, Yang X, Lin D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: First-episode drug-naïve depressive disorders have high heterogeneity in clinical features, and there is still room for in-depth exploration of the correlation with serum cortisol levels. This study aimed to explore the correlation between hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) function in the acute phase of first-episode drug-naïve major depressive disorder (MDD) and clinical features evaluated by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-24) and the Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Patients with first-episode drug-naïve MDD in the acute phase meeting the DSM-V diagnostic criteria were selected as the study group, and healthy individuals matched for gender and age were recruited as the control group. Serum cortisol levels were measured in both groups, and patients in the MDD group were evaluated using HAMD-24 and SDS.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The serum cortisol level in the MDD group(307.03 ± 77.80 nmol/L) was significantly higher than that in the healthy control group(261.13 ± 58.15 nmol/L) (Z-Value = -3.539, P < 0.05). The serum cortisol level showed a positive correlation trend (ρ > 0) with the anxiety factor, cognitive impairment factor, retardation factor, despair factor, total HAMD score, and SDS score, with statistical significance (p < 0.05). It showed a negative correlation trend (ρ < 0) with the sleep factor, without statistical significance (p > 0.05). It also showed a positive correlation trend (ρ > 0) with the weight factor and diurnal variation factor, without statistical significance (p > 0.05).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: A significant increase in serum cortisol level can serve as one of the biological indicators for predicting the core symptom clusters and disease severity of MDD. Regulation of The HPA axis cortisol pathway may have potential value in alleviating MDD symptoms.

items.title: Multiscale EEG network alterations in adolescents with depressive symptoms: static-dynamic connectivity, topological features, and exploratory scalp-level network hubs.
items.authors: Hou L, Chen M, Yang J, Ren Y, Peng T, Li Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescence is a critical period for brain network development and a vulnerable stage for the emergence of depressive symptoms Although altered brain connectivity has been reported in depression, the multiscale organization of resting-state EEG networks in adolescents with depressive symptoms (ADS) remains insufficiently understood. In particular, conventional network analyses are often constrained by fixed thresholding strategies and single-level observations, which may obscure scale-specific and topology-related abnormalities.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Eyes-closed resting-state EEG data were collected from 96 adolescents with depressive symptoms and 154 healthy controls. A data-driven adaptive thresholding strategy was used to construct subject-specific brain functional networks. Static functional connectivity, dynamic functional connectivity, and higher-order topological features were analyzed across macro-, meso-, and micro-scale levels. A multidimensional abnormality convergence matrix was further constructed to explore the spatial correspondence between network abnormalities and exploratory scalp-level neuromodulation hubs.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: ADS showed scale-dependent abnormalities in brain network organization. At the macro- and meso-scale levels, abnormalities were mainly characterized by theta-band static hyperconnectivity, particularly involving central-region networks, together with reduced dynamic transition flexibility involving prefrontal systems. Micro-scale analysis further localized these alterations to specific connections and nodes. Static connectivity abnormalities were mainly observed along the midline prefrontal-central axis, including Fp1/Fz-FCz connections, whereas dynamic instability was mainly found in right prefrontal-occipital pathways, including Fp2/F4-Oz connections. Higher-order topological analysis indicated vulnerability of right prefrontal nodes, particularly Fp2 and F4. The convergence matrix showed spatial overlap between abnormal network features and the approximate scalp projections of prefrontal neuromodulation sites, while also identifying FCz and Oz as additional nodes that may warrant further investigation.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study provides a multiscale EEG network characterization of adolescents with depressive symptoms. The findings suggest that ADS-related network alterations may involve coexisting compensatory connectivity changes, reduced dynamic flexibility, and focal topological vulnerability. These results may help refine network-level features and provide hypothesis-generating computational references for future studies exploring individualized neuromodulation strategies in adolescents with depressive symptoms.

Static connectivity abnormalities were mainly observed along the midline prefrontal-central axis, including Fp1/Fz-FCz connections, whereas dynamic instability was mainly found in right prefrontal-occipital pathways, including Fp2/F4-Oz connections. Higher-order topological analysis indicated vulnerability of right prefrontal nodes, particularly Fp2 and F4. The convergence matrix showed spatial overlap between abnormal network features and the approximate scalp projections of prefrontal neuromodulation sites, while also identifying FCz and Oz as additional nodes that may warrant further investigation.

This study provides a multiscale EEG network characterization of adolescents with depressive symptoms. The findings suggest that ADS-related network alterations may involve coexisting compensatory connectivity changes, reduced dynamic flexibility, and focal topological vulnerability. These results may help refine network-level features and provide hypothesis-generating computational references for future studies exploring individualized neuromodulation strategies in adolescents with depressive symptoms.

items.title: Behavioral and psychosocial indicators for depression and anxiety risk stratification among college students: development and external validation of a machine-learning-assisted framework.
items.authors: Mao K, He Y, Yin X, Lin L, Zheng Y, Hu G.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Depression and anxiety symptoms are common among college students. Behavioral and psychosocial indicators may support preventive campus mental health work, but risk-stratification frameworks require external validation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We developed a construct-level model-explanation framework using questionnaire data from a development sample. The cleaned dataset included 1,267 students; internal-validation analyses included 1,096 students for depression risk and 1,095 for anxiety risk. Risk was defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) or Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) score of 10 or higher. The primary Feature set C random-forest (RF) pipelines integrated demographic, traditional, and emerging behavioral and psychosocial indicators. Fold-specific preprocessing and percentile cutoffs were used for internal validation. Locked pipelines were applied without retraining, predictor reselection, optimization, recalibration, or threshold adjustment to an independent university sample of 1,468 students.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: External area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC), and Brier scores were 0.813 (95% CI, 0.776-0.848), 0.402 (0.325-0.491), and 0.090 (0.083-0.098), respectively, for depression and 0.809 (0.765-0.851), 0.205 (0.144-0.300), and 0.063 (0.056-0.070), respectively, for anxiety. Ordinary participant-level bootstrap was the primary approach, with stratified bootstrap as a sensitivity analysis. Depression calibration was close to the prevalence baseline (Brier 0.091; intercept -0.668; slope 1.401), whereas anxiety showed miscalibration (Brier 0.063 vs. baseline 0.051; intercept -1.227; slope 1.102). The models supported external discrimination and risk ranking but did not validate individual absolute-risk probabilities or clinical thresholds.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Behavioral and psychosocial indicators supported externally validated risk stratification in an independent university sample. Anxiety-risk findings should be interpreted as preliminary because the number of positive cases was limited. Further evaluation is needed before wider implementation.

items.title: How much can music listening habits tell us about mental health? An interpretable machine learning benchmark using genre preference and self-reported anxiety, depression, insomnia, and obsessive-compulsive symptoms.
items.authors: Li Y, Ren B.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Music listening is widely believed to index mental health, and this belief underwrites applications inferring psychological state from listening records. We estimated how much information musical preference and listening behavior carry about self-reported distress, and tested whether classification accuracy reported for a widely reused public dataset reflects discriminative skill or class imbalance.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of the Music and Mental Health (MxMH) survey ( n  = 736), a self-selected online convenience sample collected in 2022 with no probability sampling frame, no design weights, and no measurement of gender, geography, education, income, or clinical history. In total, 42 predictors covering genre exposure, favorite genre, streaming platform, listening hours, tempo preference, and musical engagement were modeled against four single-item, unvalidated self-anchored distress ratings, a secondary composite index, and a self-attributed judgment of whether music improves mental health. Elastic net, support vector machine, random forest, and gradient boosting models were compared against mean-prediction and majority-class baselines using nested cross-validation, corrected t -tests, permutation nulls, and Shapley additive explanations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Out-of-sample explanatory power was small. Random forests achieved cross-validated R ^2 values of 0.068 for depression, 0.058 for the composite index, 0.032 for anxiety, and 0.006 or below for insomnia and obsessive-compulsive ratings, exceeding the mean-prediction baseline for all outcomes except insomnia ( p  = 0.157). Permutation tests separated depression, anxiety, the composite, and obsessive-compulsive ratings from noise, but not insomnia ( p  = 0.198). For the self-attributed effect of music, the best classifier reached 74.7% accuracy against a majority-class baseline of 74.5% ( p  = 0.896), while balanced accuracy peaked at 0.551 and the Matthews correlation coefficient at 0.135.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Listening habits carry a real but very small signal about self-reported distress, and apparent accuracy on this dataset is an artifact of class imbalance. Musical preference is not a usable individual-level marker of psychological state. These estimates come from a single, heavily reused, non-representative convenience sample with unvalidated single-item outcomes and no demographic weighting variables, so they characterize this archive rather than any defined population and require independent replication before any specific effect size is treated as settled. Dataset: MxMH survey, Kaggle.

items.title: The effects of physical exercise on executive function, internalizing symptoms and externalizing symptoms in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Shi J, Zheng X, Wang W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The aim of this study is to comprehensively assess the potential effects of physical exercise on executive function, internalizing symptoms and externalizing symptoms in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and to explore the moderating factors influencing these effects.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We performed a systematic search of six databases (including Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, PsycNET, the Cochrane Library and SPORTDiscus). Data analysis was performed using R software, and a meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model to estimate the pooled effect size. In addition, subgroup analyses and meta-regression were conducted to explore potential moderating factors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 25 randomised controlled trials involving 1,116 participants were included. With low certainty of evidence, the pooled effect of inhibitory control was statistically significant ( g = 0.45, p < 0.01). With very low certainty of evidence, the pooled effect of internalizing symptoms was statistically significant ( g = 0.97, p = 0.03). The pooled effects of cognitive flexibility ( g = 0.69, p = 0.054), working memory ( g = 0.28, p = 0.10), and externalizing symptoms ( g = 0.64, p = 0.29) did not reach statistical significance, all rated as very low certainty of evidence.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Physical exercise may be positively associated with inhibitory control in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, the effects of interventions show high heterogeneity, have wide confidence intervals, and exhibit limited stability.

sections.text: PROSPERO CRD420261380631.

items.title: Mapping evidence on support networks and their impact on postnatal teenage mothers' mental health in a global context: A scoping review.
items.authors: Sikhwari R, Mulaudzi FM, Foromo R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Postnatal teenage mothers faced unique mental health challenges because of the combined effects of adolescence and early motherhood. While the importance of support networks was acknowledged, a comprehensive understanding of their influence across global and African contexts remains limited.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This scoping review aimed to map existing research on support networks available to postnatal teenage mothers and explored their impact on mental health outcomes. The review included studies from healthcare and community settings across South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, United Kingdom, Indonesia, Turkey, Canada, Mozambique, Brazil, Iran, Jordan and Nairobi.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: A systematic search identified 15 articles published between 2020 and 2025 from Web of Science, EBSCOhost, ProQuest, Google Scholar, and PubMed. Studies using qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods approaches were included after Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-guided screening of 1242 records, with data thematically synthesised.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Ten main themes emerged from thematic analysis of the included studies, namely lack of family support, lack of healthcare professional support, digital support, financial support, emotional support, physical support, absence and accessibility of partner or spousal support, lack of social support, mental conditions and support in developed settings. Family's emotional or practical support protected against postpartum depression and anxiety, while partner involvement and financial stability significantly influenced outcomes. Digital support showed promise where formal services lacked accessibility.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Integrated, adolescent-sensitive support networks proved critical for promoting mental health among postnatal teenage mothers. Addressing service gaps, social stigma and strengthening family or partner support remained essential for improving well-being in this vulnerable group.

sections.heading: Contribution
sections.text: This review mapped support network types and their mental health impacts, providing evidence for targeted policy development and clinical interventions tailored to teenage mothers' unique needs across diverse global contexts.

items.title: Classification of Children With Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Typically Developed Children Using Toro's Gyrification Index: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Ediri Arachchi W, Jayasinghe E, Piyumali H, Senanayake G, Thuduvage V, Mudalige I.

sections.heading: Background and aim
sections.text: Attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder of childhood, with a higher prevalence in males. It is characterized by deficits in attention, impulsivity, and/or hyperactivity. Aberrant cortical gyrification patterns are hypothesized to be associated with the neural substrates and clinical manifestations of ADHD. This study aimed to employ pattern classification analysis to assess the discriminative potential of cortical gyrification in classifying children with ADHD and typically developing (TD) children.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Three-dimensional T1-weighted images were acquired from 35 male children with ADHD and 30 male TD children using a 3 Tesla MRI scanner. The Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12) was used to compute Toro's gyrification index for each subject. The statistical analysis was performed using a general linear model, with age included as a covariate, and the results were corrected for multiple comparisons using family-wise error correction. A linear support vector machine classifier was trained on the training dataset and tested using k-fold cross-validation, with one-fold left out in each iteration.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Children with ADHD demonstrated bilaterally increased cortical gyrification in the middle temporal gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus, and the banks of the superior temporal sulcus (banksSTS). Additionally, increased gyrification was observed in the left superior temporal gyrus. Pattern classification analysis revealed that Toro's gyrification index discriminated between children with ADHD and TD children with an accuracy of 86.15%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings suggest that Toro's gyrification index captures ADHD-related morphological alterations and may represent a promising neuroimaging biomarker for distinguishing ADHD from typically developing brains.

items.title: Psychological Experience and Coping Strategies of Caregivers for Chinese Adolescents With Non-Suicidal Self-Injury: A Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Studies.
items.authors: Wu H, Zhao Y, Fan R, Pan H, Yu T, Hu Y.

sections.heading: Background and aims
sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) among adolescents, including those with comorbid affective disorders, imposes substantial psychological distress and caregiving burden in mainland China. This qualitative meta-synthesis aimed to systematically synthesize evidence regarding the psychological experiences, coping strategies, and support needs of caregivers of adolescents with NSSI in mainland China to inform culturally adapted, family-centered interventions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Guided by ENTREQ and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, seven English and Chinese databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, CBM, Wanfang Data) were systematically searched from inception to July 29, 2026. Qualitative studies examining caregivers of adolescents (aged 8-18 years) with NSSI in mainland China were included. Quality was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and data were synthesized using Thomas and Harden's thematic synthesis approach.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Twenty studies involving 322 caregivers were synthesized. Caregivers of adolescents with NSSI in mainland China were interpreted as undergoing a dynamic, iterative pattern of psychological distress across three analytical themes: (1) Moral panic and self-attribution of blame, where initial crisis and moral self-blame induced stigma and delayed formal help-seeking; (2) The tug-of-war between safety surveillance and family autonomy, characterized by hypervigilance and a fear-driven coping cycle involving verbal aggression, coercive restraint, and blind indulgence; and (3) Institutional isolation and relapse trauma, marked by school rejection, service fragmentation, and survival achieved by recalibrating goals to negotiated, limited stability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Caregivers navigate a trajectory of accumulating distress shaped by moral reasoning, fear-based reactivity, and institutional invalidation. Clinical pathways should integrate routine caregiver assessments, phase-matched psychoeducation and skills training, and cross-sector collaboration to address caregiver isolation.

items.title: Retrospectively Reported Psychological Distress Among Nurses and Nursing Students Following the War Between Iran and Israel: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Farsi Z, Afaghi E, Pakdin F, Taghaei F, Negarandeh R.

sections.heading: Background and aim
sections.text: Crises can significantly affect healthcare professionals' mental health. This study aimed to examine retrospectively reported psychological experiences among Iranian nurses and nursing students in relation to the 12-Day War between Iran and Israel.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Iran in 2025. We recruited 484 nurses and nursing students using a convenience sampling approach. A questionnaire based on the General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-28) was used to assess somatic symptoms, anxiety/insomnia, social dysfunction, and severe depression. Higher GHQ-28 scores indicate greater psychological distress and poorer mental health.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Over half of participants ( n  = 272, 56.2%) had GHQ-28 scores above the conventional cutoff of 23; however, this proportion should not be interpreted as the prevalence of psychological distress during the war because the questionnaire was administered retrospectively. The average GHQ score was 27.58 ± 15.04. Longer sleep duration ( B  = - 0.908, 95% CI [ - 1.682 to -0.135], β  = -0.096, p  = 0.02) and dormitory residence ( B  = - 4.876, 95% CI [ - 9.372 to -0.381], β  = -0.120, p  = 0.03) were associated with lower GHQ-28 scores. Male participants had lower GHQ-28 scores than female participants ( B  = - 5.556, 95% CI [ - 8.256 to -2.856], β  = -0.179, p  < 0.001). Participants who had no exposure to explosions (B = - 3.049, 95% CI [ - 5.598 to -0.501], β  = -0.102, p  = 0.02) had lower GHQ-28 scores. In the additional model, initiation or increase of sedative medication was positively associated with GHQ-28 scores ( B  = 11.780, 95% CI [7.997 to 15.564], β  = 0.280, p  < 0.001). The main explanatory model explained 17.4% of the variance in GHQ-28 scores, while the additional model including clinical and help-seeking variables explained 28.6%.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Retrospectively reported GHQ-28 scores were associated with demographic, occupational, and conflict-related characteristics among nurses and nursing students. However, given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal. Therefore, supporting the mental health of nurses and nursing students may be important for maintaining the quality of care in regions affected by military conflict. Longitudinal studies are suggested to assess changes in GHQ-28 dimensions.

items.title: Problem gambling and its correlates among treatment-seeking opioid users at a tertiary care center: A cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Biswas T, Mishra P, Patra C, Mishra BR, Parmar A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Gambling is a major public health concern worldwide. Problem gambling refers to excessive gambling behaviors associated with negative health and socioeconomic consequences. Studies have described a strong association between problem gambling and substance use disorders (SUDs), with shared psychosocial and neurobiological vulnerabilities. However, comorbidity research in opioid use disorder (OUD) is limited.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To estimate the burden of problem gambling and its correlates among patients with OUD.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional observational study, over one year, included 125 adult men (mean age: 33.7 ± 10.5 years) with OUD seeking treatment at a tertiary-care center. Sociodemographic and clinical variables of the participants were collected using a predetermined structured proforma, and problem gambling was assessed using the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS).

sections.heading: Results

items.title: Applying machine learning to investigate future life-oriented predictors of adolescents' near-term suicidal ideation.
items.authors: Lee DE, Lawrence O, Shin KE, Wang SB, Cha CB.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescents contemplating suicide consider both the discontinuation and continuation of their lives. Yet prior research has mainly focused on what suicidal youth want to escape from (i.e., distress-oriented predictors) rather than what may keep them living into the future. This study applies machine learning (ML) to examine how adolescents' momentary Future Life-Oriented (FLO) processes predict their near-term changes in suicidal ideation (SI).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Adolescents (N = 121; 15-17 years) completed a 14-day, 5x/day smartphone-based ecological momentary assessment protocol, reporting on a range of FLO predictors (e.g., vividness, importance, emotional valence of future life events), distress-oriented predictors (e.g., prior SI, stressors, affect), and SI. ML algorithms were trained on time-series data to predict future SI based on FLO and distress-oriented predictors. To identify optimal temporal prediction windows, we implemented a sliding-window approach and compared models across multiple temporal frames.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Models including FLO variables significantly improved prediction of subsequent SI (AUC = 0.880) relative to models using prior SI (AUC = 0.783) alone or prior SI with stress/affect (AUC = 0.781). The best-performing model (Random Forest; AUC = 0.956) achieved optimal prediction using seven prior observations to forecast SI two timepoints ahead (avg. 11h). SHAP analyses identified prior SI and two FLO variables (desire to live, future thought uncontrollability) as the most influential predictors of SI.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Adolescents' momentary FLO processes meaningfully enhance near-term prediction of SI, highlighting a potentially promising collection of modifiable targets for suicide prevention.

items.title: Temporal dynamics of premenstrual dysphoric disorder revealed through predictive symptom networks.
items.authors: Schleimann-Jensen E, Sundström-Poromaa I, Hoppe JM, Engel S, Kiesner J, Comasco E.

sections.text: Temporal dynamics of psychiatric symptoms challenge researchers and clinicians due to their inherent unpredictability. The cyclical on-off nature of symptoms linked to physiological rhythms, such as the menstrual cycle, provides a unique window to apply temporal and dynamic modeling of psychiatric symptoms. This can be studied in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, a female hormone-triggered condition characterized by cyclical symptoms. Yet intra-individual temporal patterns and dynamics of these symptoms remain unknown. Here we show that individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder differ widely in symptom timing, severity, and persistence, clustering into distinct temporal symptom profiles. Dynamic modelling uncovers temporal order among core psychiatric symptoms, with anxiety emerging as a central symptom in the unfolding of affective dysregulation. Depression shows the strongest predictive associations with subsequent severity of the other core symptoms, while irritability predicts the severity of depression at the longest time-interval. These temporal symptom dynamics reveal mechanistic psychoneuroendocrine pathways and inform precision, time-sensitive interventions for the mental health of individuals with premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

items.title: Suicide risk factors in nursing students: Depressive symptoms, academic burnout and academic efficacy after the pandemic.
items.authors: Ardiles-Irarrázabal RA, Pérez-Díaz PA, Pérez-González JC, Valdivia-Rojas Y, Valencia-Contrera M.

sections.text: The present study analyze the prevalence and factors associated with suicide risk in nursing students in the post-pandemic context, considering academic burnout, academic engagement, and symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress as predictors. through a cross-sectional and correlational study conducted in a public university in Northern Chile. with a168 nursing undergraduates' sample. Validated instruments were administered, including the Beck Hopelessness Scale, the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale, the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Student Survey, and the DASS-21. Descriptive analyses, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression were conducted. A total of 11.31% of students met the predefined BHS threshold for elevated suicide-related risk. In the same sample, symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress showed high prevalence rates. Suicide risk was negatively associated with vigor and dedication, while positively associated with low academic efficacy and depression. The regression model explained 54% of the variance in suicide risk (Adj.R² = 0.54; p < 0.001), with Depression (β = 4.04), Vigor (β = 0.63), Academic Efficacy (β = 0.88), and the interaction between Depression and Vigor (β = -0.69) being significant predictors in the model. Suicide risk in nursing students transcends traditional clinical factors, as it is shaped by the interaction between personal resources and mental health symptoms. These findings underscore the need for prevention and psychosocial support programs in nursing schools.

items.title: Poor sleep quality and anxiety in patients with diabetes mellitus and its association with glycemic control: A cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Baghdad W, Satté A, El Harrati O, El Brouzi MY, Bernoussi Z, Raggabi A, Hmamouchi I, El Omri N, Mekouar F, Mesfioui A, Sqalli Houssaini Y, El Hessni A.

sections.text: Sleep is crucial for maintaining physical and mental health, and poor sleep quality is associated with an increased risk of metabolic, cognitive, and cardiovascular diseases. This study aimed to assess sleep quality and factors associated with poor sleep quality, such as mental disorders, especially anxiety, in adult patients with type 2 diabetes in Morocco. A cross-sectional study was conducted on patients with type 2 diabetes, using random selection, aged 39-85, in the clinical neurophysiology and internal medicine department of the Mohammed V Military Instruction Hospital, between 30/09/2024 and 30/12/2024. The questionnaire comprised demographic data, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7). Descriptive tests, independent two-sample t-tests, chi-square tests, and logistic regressions were performed using Jamovi version 2.6.2. Out of the 120 participants, the mean age of our patients was 65.4 ± 9.32 years, of whom 66.67% were women. The mean PSQI score was 9.18 ± 3.73, and the mean GAD-7 score was 8.0 ± 6.11. Poor sleep quality was reported in 84.2% of participants, while a binary logistic regression analysis revealed that poor sleep quality was not significantly associated with high HbA1c, but rather was highly significant with age and GAD-7. The study reveals that poor sleep quality is common among type 2 diabetic patients in Morocco, and is strongly associated with generalized anxiety disorders. These findings underscore the crucial role of psychological factors in diabetes management. They highlight the need for a comprehensive and integrated approach that takes into account not only biomedical aspects but also the psychological and behavioral dimensions of patients.

items.title: Prevalence and determinants of readmission at a tertiary psychiatric hospital in Zanzibar.
items.authors: Abdallah AK, Ottaru TA, Moshiro C.
items.journal: The South African journal of psychiatry : SAJP : the journal of the Society of Psychiatrists of South Africa

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychiatric readmission is a global concern, leading to poorer clinical outcomes and higher healthcare costs. In Tanzania, where mental health services operate within a resource-constrained health system, repeated psychiatric admissions may place additional pressure on already limited services. However, local evidence on psychiatric readmission remains limited.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: To determine the prevalence of psychiatric readmission and its determinants among psychiatric patients admitted to a tertiary psychiatric hospital in Unguja, Zanzibar.

sections.heading: Setting
sections.text: A tertiary psychiatric referral hospital in Unguja, Zanzibar, serving patients across Unguja and Pemba islands.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among psychiatric patients 18 years and older admitted between June 2024 and August 2024. Data were collected through interviewer-administered questionnaires. Modified Poisson regression with robust error variance was used to identify factors associated with psychiatric readmission.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 311 patients (mean age 36, standard deviation [s.d.] = 11 years; females 52.4%; schizophrenia 32.5%) were enrolled. The prevalence of psychiatric readmission within 3 months was 58.5% (n = 182). Readmission was associated with age group 30-39 years (adjusted prevalence ratio [APR] = 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.16-1.84, p -value [ p ] = 0.001), schizophrenia (APR = 1.23; CI: 1.00-1.50, p = 0.041), bipolar disorders (APR = 1.69; CI: 1.26-2.26, p < 0.001), higher education (APR = 1.61; CI: 1.16-2.22, p = 0.010), history of physical abuse (APR = 1.49; CI: 1.16-2.22, p < 0.001), and being prescribed both oral and injectable medications (APR = 1.46; CI: 1.37-2.20, p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: There is a high psychiatric readmission rate in Zanzibar. Interventions should focus on high-risk groups, particularly middle-aged individuals and those requiring combination treatment to break the cycle of readmission and promote long-term mental health recovery.

sections.heading: Contribution
sections.text: This study provides evidence on psychiatric readmission in Zanzibar and identifies high-risk groups requiring targeted post-discharge intervention in low-resource psychiatric settings.

items.title: Repurposing incretin-based therapies for alcohol use disorder: a systematic review of efficacy and safety relative to standard pharmacotherapies in a recent comparative context.
items.authors: Alevizopoulos AG, Vasilakos V, Kritikos I, Alevizopoulou M, Korompoki E, Psaltopoulou T, Paschou SA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) affects millions worldwide, but current treatments, such as disulfiram, naltrexone, acamprosate, and topiramate, have limitations in efficacy and tolerability. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), commonly used for diabetes and obesity, may offer a new approach by targeting brain pathways involved in alcohol cravings.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This review aims to systematically evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RAs and other incretin-based therapies in treating AUD within a recent comparative context, alongside standard pharmacotherapies.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Systematic review.

sections.heading: Data sources and methods
sections.text: A comprehensive literature review was conducted by searching the PubMed/Medline, Web of Science, and Scopus databases from February through June 2025. The studies included were either randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or observational studies, written in English. Studies were selected based on their evaluation of GLP-1 RAs or comparator drugs in reducing alcohol consumption or related outcomes in patients with AUD.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The selected 12 studies correspond to a population of 95,004 participants, but only 663 were from RCTs, while the majority were from a single registry cohort. Emerging data suggest GLP-1 RAs may reduce heavy drinking days, particularly in individuals with a higher BMI. Furthermore, observational analyses indicate a potential association between GLP-1 RA use and reduced alcohol-related hospitalizations, while metabolic data suggest biologically plausible, albeit unconfirmed, hepatoprotective effects.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: While the large, aggregated sample size highlights the therapeutic promise of GLP-1 RAs for AUD, particularly for patients with metabolic comorbidities, the heavy reliance on observational data precludes claims of clinical equivalence with established pharmacotherapies. Appropriately powered, dedicated RCTs are required to confirm direct efficacy and long-term safety.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: Not registered.

items.title: Case Report: Hyperactive delirium with psychotic symptoms associated with severe hypothyroidism during pembrolizumab therapy. Complete remission after levothyroxine and no recurrence after pembrolizumab rechallenge.
items.authors: Vieira Fregolente E, Bühler S, Lahr J.

sections.text: Thyroid dysfunction is a common adverse event during pembrolizumab therapy, but severe hypothyroidism accompanied by acute neuropsychiatric symptoms is rare. We present the case of a 78-year-old woman with metastatic colorectal cancer who developed agitation, hallucinations, and confusion three months after initiation of Pembrolizumab. Evaluation revealed profound hypothyroidism (TSH 37.9 mU/L, free T3 <0.60 pmol/L and free T4 <0.5 pmol/L) and moderate hyponatremia without acute findings on neuroimaging. Levothyroxine therapy led to complete remission of neuropsychiatric symptoms, and pembrolizumab was safely restarted with close monitoring and no recurrence. This case underscores the importance of assessing thyroid function in acute psychiatric presentations during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and supports cautious rechallenge after stabilization. Severe hypothyroidism was considered a major contributor, although a multifactorial delirium, including the contribution of hyponatremia and the absence of CSF/EEG evaluation, cannot be excluded.

items.title: Effects of different electrical stimulation on depression: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
items.authors: Chai J, Li S, Huang J, Yao S, Zhou L, Chen X, Liu F, Ji C, Chen H, Tan S, Li R, Ma R, Li S, Zhao S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric disorder characterised by persistent low mood and anhedonia, substantially impairing quality of life. Conventional treatments show variable efficacy and tolerability, with high post-discontinuation relapse rates. Electrical stimulation has emerged as an alternative intervention, but comparative efficacy and safety of different modalities remain uncertain. This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to synthesise evidence and quantitatively compare electrical stimulation approaches for depression.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search of 13 databases was conducted for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) published from inception to 16 July 2026. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with the GRADE framework. Frequentist network meta-analysis was performed using STATA 18.0. Publication bias was assessed via funnel plot inspection, and sensitivity analyses examined the robustness of findings.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 33 RCTs involving 2,664 participants and nine electrical stimulation modalities were included. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that electrical stimulation was associated with a significantly improved clinical response rate (OR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.50 to 5.16) and a reduction in depressive symptom severity (SMD = -0.90, 95% CI -1.27 to -0.54) among patients with depression, along with a favourable safety profile (OR = 0.88, 95% CI 0.52 to 1.49). However, therapeutic effects varied across modalities. Specifically, Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) ranked highest for improving the clinical response rate (SUCRA = 99.9%; OR = 4.12, 95% CI 3.08 to 5.16), whereas transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) ranked highest for reducing the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) score (SUCRA = 71.3%; SMD = -1.70, 95% CI -2.80 to -0.60). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these results.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Electrical stimulation is associated with improved clinical response rates and reduced depressive symptom severity in patients with depression, and is generally well tolerated. Among the modalities examined, taVNS demonstrated a relative advantage in improving clinical response, while tDCS showed a relative advantage in alleviating depressive symptom severity. However, given the low certainty of the evidence underpinning these findings, they require confirmation in larger, higher-quality randomised controlled trials.

items.title: FOOTBIKE exercise enhances mental health through improved executive function in university students.
items.authors: Qi S, Yu J, Wei Z, Yin L, Wei L.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: This study investigated the effects of FOOTBIKE exercise on mental health and executive function in university students, aiming to explore a novel exercise-based approach for mental health promotion in higher education settings.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Sixty healthy undergraduate students from Shandong Sport University were randomly assigned to either an experimental group ( n = 30) or a control group ( i = 30). The experimental group completed an 8-week FOOTBIKE intervention consisting of three 60-min sessions per week, while the control group maintained routine activities and regular physical education classes. Pre- and post-intervention assessments utilized an AI-based physiological and psychological monitoring system, a 2-back working memory task, and a Go/No-Go inhibitory control task.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Following the FOOTBIKE exercise intervention, the experimental group exhibited significantly reduced anxiety and inhibition indices compared to the control group ( p < 0.05), together with significantly enhancing reaction capacity and stress resilience ( p < 0.05). Reaction times in both the 2-back working memory task and the Go/No-Go inhibitory control task were also significantly reduced after FOOTBIKE training ( p < 0.05), indicating improvements in cognitive processing efficiency and inhibitory control. There was a significant group 7 time interaction effect on the inhibition index, reaction times in the 2-back task, and reaction times in the Go/No-Go task. In contrast, no significant differences were observed in conventional physiological indicators or task accuracy, suggesting that the psychological benefits of FOOTBIKE exercise may be more closely related to cognitive and emotional regulatory adaptations than to general physiological conditioning alone. Furthermore, random forest analysis identified reaction speed, anxiety index, stress tolerance, and executive-function-related variables as important contributors distinguishing the experimental group after intervention, which was further supported by principal component analysis.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: FOOTBIKE exercise enhances mental health primarily through improvements in executive function, emotional regulation, cognitive responsiveness, and stress adaptation capacity. As a cognitively engaging, enjoyable, safe, and easily scalable form of physical activity, FOOTBIKE may represent a promising intervention strategy for university physical education curricula and mental health promotion programs.

items.title: Fifty years at the addiction bench and bedside: from withdrawal syndromes to adaptive brain states.
items.authors: Gold MS.

sections.text: Over the past half-century, addiction medicine has moved from moral and symptom-based explanations toward a neuroscience of adaptation, learning, motivation, and recovery. This Perspective uses several linked translational programs-opioid withdrawal and the locus coeruleus, cocaine dependence and dopamine, environmental drug exposure, physician health, and food reward-to illustrate how observations at the bedside can generate mechanistic studies and how laboratory findings can, in turn, change treatment and public health. LC stimulation produced signs and symptoms that looked to me like opioid withdrawal. So, we thought that noradrenergic hyperactivity in opioid withdrawal caused symptoms, and while methadone or morphine could treat these, we could also treat them with a non-opioid, clonidine. Earlier noradrenergic interventions had been attempted with limited clinical success. Our work provided the first hypothesis-driven, double-blind, placebo-controlled demonstration that a non-opioid medication could suppress the acute human opioid withdrawal syndrome. This mechanism-based treatment was greeted with considerable interest because some clinicians had assumed that any medication capable of reversing opioid withdrawal distress must itself be an opioid. Clonidine and later lofexidine did just that and facilitated transition to naltrexone. Recognition that cocaine could produce compulsive use without a dramatic physical withdrawal syndrome helped shift the field toward reward circuitry, craving, pathological attraction, anhedonia, and relapse. Studies of tobacco, cannabis, and opioid smoke broadened prevention by showing that involuntary second- and third-hand exposure can be biologically detected and, most clearly for tobacco, can produce biologically meaningful effects. Third-hand exposure refers to residual drug-related contaminants that persist on indoor surfaces, dust, clothing, or other materials after active smoking has ended. Contemporary work on neuromodulation, exercise, psychedelics, and GLP-1 metabolic-reward pathways extends the same translational logic. Addiction is best understood as an acquired adaptive brain state supported by anti-survival or bad learning, development, and environment; recovery is active neurobehavioral relearning, not simply detoxification or drug clearance. Public health should therefore join brain sciences, work to delay initiation, identify emerging risk before a severe substance use disorder develops, prevent involuntary exposure, and provide rapid access to mechanism-based treatment, recovery-supportive environments, and outcomes measured over 5 years or longer.

items.title: Lived experiences, barriers, and facilitators of voluntary non-suicidal self-injury disclosure among adolescents who have disclosed: a qualitative systematic review protocol.
items.authors: He X, Xu X, Huang H, Peng J, Yang B, Huang J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is common among adolescents and often remains concealed because of shame and stigma. Voluntary disclosure can provide access to support, but emotional and interpersonal concerns shape the decision to disclose. This review will synthesize disclosure experiences, barriers, and facilitators reported by adolescents who have voluntarily disclosed NSSI at least once.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Primary qualitative studies and separately extractable qualitative components of mixed-methods studies involving adolescents aged 10-19 years will be eligible. Searches will cover PubMed, Embase, APA PsycINFO, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection. China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database will also be searched. Coverage will extend from inception through 31 March 2026, inclusive, without language restrictions; formal searches have not yet been executed. Gray literature, reference lists, and forward citations will also be searched. Two human reviewers will independently select studies, appraise them using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) qualitative checklist, and extract findings. Findings will be synthesized using JBI meta-aggregation, with confidence assessed using ConQual.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The synthesis will examine disclosure decisions, recipients' responses, and subsequent experiences from adolescents' perspectives. Findings may inform clinical, school, and family support for voluntary NSSI disclosure.

sections.heading: Systematic review registration
sections.text: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261355173, identifier: CRD420261355173.
